papers.title: Benchmarking Machine Learning for Chaotic Three-Body Dynamics in Astrophysics
papers.summary: Machine learning (ML) and generative AI have recently made impressive progress in understanding physics. We explore a hierarchy of prediction problems stemming from chaotic three-body systems and benchmark existing ML approaches, including general-purpose prediction algorithms and those that build on top of foundational physics models. We first simulate the trajectories of triple systems near the critical boundary of stable/unstable initial conditions. We then design a hierarchy of learning tasks, focusing mainly on two broad problems: stability prediction and trajectory prediction. The former classifies whether a given triple system has diverged or not up to a specific horizon, while the latter predicts the exact trajectory, both given suitable input features. We benchmark a range of ML approaches, from simple regression methods to state-of-the-art foundational physics models, across these tasks, and compare them against astrophysical methods such as the Mardling-Aarseth stability criterion. Our experiments reveal a clear order of task difficulties in chaotic three-body dynamics: early dynamics enable strong stability prediction, while precise long-horizon trajectory forecasting remains difficult. Code and dataset are publicly available at https://github.com/Simonwan03/ThreeBodyMLBench.
papers.title_ja: 天体物理学におけるカオス的な三体力学の機械学習ベンチマーク
papers.summary_ja: カオス的な三体系における安定性予測と軌道予測のタスク階層を設計し、既存の機械学習手法をベンチマークした。汎用的な予測アルゴリズムから物理基礎モデルまでを比較し、天体物理学の既存手法（Mardling-Aarseth基準）とも対比した。実験の結果、初期動態からの安定性予測は高精度だが、長期の正確な軌道予測は依然として困難であることが明らかになった。コードとデータセットは公開されている。
papers.relevance_reason: 軌道力学・三体問題とMLの組み合わせであり、ユーザーの関心と完全に一致する。

papers.title: PINNeval: A Comprehensive Evaluation Standard for Physics-Informed Neural Networks
papers.summary: The Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) literature has produced a rapidly expanding catalogue of methods. We divide a PINN training pipeline systematically into four components and observe that many existing benchmarks study these components in isolation. These components are domain-importance adaptation, loss balancing, neural network architecture, and optimization scheme. Moreover, the studies set the surrounding and not considered components of the pipeline to a minimal default that is no longer representative of current best practice approaches. Conclusions drawn under such conditions may not transfer to competitive pipelines. In this work, we propose a new evaluation protocol that (1) treats the four components as an integrated system; (2) crucially requires competitive implementations of the components not under investigation; (3) specifies the metrics and reporting format; and (4) is accompanied by structured documentation that ensures the traceability of evaluations across studies. Based on this comprehensive protocol, we release PINNpipe, an innovative JAX package containing 18 different methods from the current literature as well as nine efficiently implemented benchmark problems. Using PINNpipe, we illustrate our evaluation protocol in relation to established benchmark studies and report results that challenge common assumptions.
papers.title_ja: PINNeval: 物理情報ニューラルネットワークのための包括的評価基準
papers.summary_ja: 物理情報ニューラルネットワーク（PINN）の既存ベンチマークがパイプラインの一部のみを評価し、他の要素を非現実的なデフォルト値で固定している問題点を指摘する。本論文では、ドメイン適応、損失バランス、アーキテクチャ、最適化手法の4要素を統合した包括的評価プロトコルを提案する。さらに、JAXベースのパッケージ「PINNpipe」を公開し、18種の手法と9つのベンチマーク問題を効率よく実装した。このプロトコルを用いた評価により、従来の研究で得られた一般的な仮定を覆す結果が示された。
papers.relevance_reason: PINNと評価手法の両方に深く関わるため

papers.title: Task-Contribution Dynamics of Adam in Physics-Informed Neural Networks: Slow-Manifold Analysis and Gradient Modulation
papers.summary: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) often suffer from imbalanced optimization of competing loss components, particularly when approximating solutions with high-frequency or multiscale features. Although existing balancing strategies have proven effective in alleviating this difficulty, the mechanisms governing the evolution of individual task contributions to Adam's parameter updates remain insufficiently understood. We introduce task-wise indicators to characterize this evolution and identify three distinct training regimes: smooth variation, intermittent spikes, and persistent oscillations. Focusing on the early smooth regime, we combine discrete-time analysis with a continuous-time singular perturbation framework under the full-batch setting and the parameter regime $(1-\beta_2)/(1-\beta_1)\ll1$. A first-order approximation of the locally attracting slow manifold reveals two factors governing the step-to-step redistribution of task contributions: curvature-related alignment disparities and differences in the coordinatewise distributions of preconditioned task gradients. Both factors involve Adam's shared second-moment estimate. Inspired by AdaTask, we propose Gradient-Modulated Adam (GMAdam), which modulates incoming task gradients using task-specific second-moment estimates. Numerical experiments on high-frequency Poisson and wave equations, the Allen-Cahn equation, and two-dimensional lid-driven cavity flow ($Re=100,400$) demonstrate consistent improvements in predictive accuracy over AdaTask at comparable computational cost.
papers.title_ja: 物理情報ニューラルネットワークにおけるAdamのタスク貢献動態：遅い多様体解析と勾配調整
papers.summary_ja: 物理情報ニューラルネットワーク（PINN）における損失項の最適化バランス問題に対し、Adamオプティマイザのタスク別勾配貢献の進化を解析した。離散時間解析と連続時間の特異摂動フレームワークを用い、初期段階のタスク貢献再分配を支配する要因として、曲率関連の整列差異と事前条件付けされたタスク勾配の座標別分布の違いを特定した。これに基づき、タスク固有の二階モーメント推定を用いて勾配を調整する新しいオプティマイザ「GMAdam」を提案した。高周波数ポアソン方程式や波方程式などの数値実験により、既存手法より予測精度が向上することを示した。
papers.relevance_reason: PINNとオプティマイザ設計の両方に深く関わるため

papers.title: Function-Space Certification for Neural Operators
papers.summary: Certifying the robustness and physical consistency of scientific machine-learning models ensures that their predictions remain reliable beyond the test set. For neural operators, which learn PDE solution operators by mapping infinite-dimensional function spaces, certification means establishing rigorous, domain-wide guarantees for their output functions. However, standard neural network (NN) verification methods are fundamentally designed for vector-to-vector mappings, and they can only certify neural operators at fixed grid resolutions and provide no guarantees over the entire domain or across another resolution. We close this gap by introducing a function-space certification framework that verifies neural operators across the entire continuous domain. We formulate interval bound propagation (IBP) and CROWN in function space, propagating upper and lower bound functions through each layer using rigorous numerical integration. In addition, we extend bound propagation to higher-order derivatives to certify PDE residuals and solution error bounds. Experiments across several neural operator architectures and scientific problems, including the 572.5-million-parameter spherical Fourier neural operator for global weather forecasting, show that our method produces tight, domain-wide guarantees efficiently, providing a foundation for trustworthy operator learning.
papers.title_ja: ニューラルオペレータのための関数空間認証
papers.summary_ja: ニューラルオペレータの予測がテストセット外でも信頼できることを保証する「関数空間認証」フレームワークを提案する。従来のベクトル間写像向け検証手法では、離散グリッド上でのみ保証でき、連続的な定義域全体や解の微分特性（PDE残差など）に対する厳密な保証が得られなかった。本手法は、区間境界伝播（IBP）やCROWNを関数空間に拡張し、厳密な数値積分を用いて各層で上下界関数を伝播させることで、定義域全体にわたる頑健性と物理的一貫性を検証する。5億7000万パラメータの球面フーリエニューラルオペレータを含む複数の科学問題で、効率的かつ緊密な保証が得られることを示し、信頼性の高いオペレータ学習の基盤を確立した。
papers.relevance_reason: ニューラルオペレータの検証・信頼性保証は、ユーザーの関心であるサロゲートモデル・物理情報NNの応用において極めて重要。

papers.title: Equidistribution of Solution Gradients in Physics-Informed Neural Networks via Coordinate Transformations
papers.summary: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) often struggle to approximate solutions with sharp gradients due to optimization difficulties and spectral bias. Motivated by the principle of gradient equidistribution from the stretching approach in grid generation, which redistributes solution gradients to reduce functional complexity, we propose Coordinate Transformation PINNs (CTPINNs), which incorporate learnable coordinate transformations to map the physical domain into a computational domain where the physical solutions become approximately affine, making them easier for neural networks to learn. We propose two constructions of the transformation: an explicit construction based on Majorants and an implicit construction based on invertable neural networks. Experimentally, the explicit construction can improve accuracy for PDEs with available explicit coordinate transformations, and the implicit construction can be combined with other advanced PINN models as an efficient plug-in module to improve performance across a range of challenging PDE benchmarks.
papers.title_ja: 座標変換による物理情報ニューラルネットワークにおける解の勾配の等分布
papers.summary_ja: 物理情報ニューラルネットワーク（PINN）が急峻な勾配を持つ解の近似に苦戦する問題に対し、座標変換を学習可能に組み込んだCTPINNsを提案する。物理領域を計算領域へ写像し、解をほぼアフィン（一次）な形に変換することで、ニューラルネットワークの学習を容易にする。明示的なMajorantsに基づく構成と、可逆ニューラルネットワークに基づく暗黙的な構成の2種類を提示し、後者は既存の高度なPINNモデルにプラグインとして組み込むことで、困難な偏微分方程式（PDE）ベンチマークにおける性能向上を実証した。
papers.relevance_reason: PINNと座標変換による最適化改善は、ユーザーの関心である物理情報ニューラルネットと手法全般に直結する。

papers.title: BiLoGo: Reducing the smoothing of localised responses in Transformer-based neural operators for sheet forming
papers.summary: Trial-and-error FE simulation of sheet forming could be computationally expensive, neural-network-based learned simulators are used to accelerate design. These simulators should accurately capture localised responses, such as thinning around sharp radii or near ribs, which determine formability. Transformer-based neural operators propagate information efficiently across the mesh but tend to smooth such localised responses. This study develops BiLoGo, a Bipartite Local-Global learned simulator with an FE-guided design that connects local node-element message passing with a Transformer-based neural operator for long-range information exchange. BiLoGo has three modules: a bidirectional node-element GraphSAGE model that learns nodal-elemental coupling on a bipartite graph and predicts each quantity on its native FE entity without interpolation; a dual-stream Transformer-based neural operator that processes blank deformation and tool contact with separate token sets, preventing localised contact information from being averaged with the whole-blank state; and a fusion and element update module that combines global and local features via gated residual fusion and updates element features conditioned on element-node kinematics. Evaluated on a dome-shaped cold forming case and two corner-shaped hot stamping cases (one with ribs), BiLoGo achieves the lowest positional and threshold-based thinning errors on all three cases compared with single-level and hierarchical graph-based models and Transformer-based neural operators. Near the ribs, the smoothing index of predicted thinning increases from 0.41-0.56 for Transformer-based neural operators to 0.94 for BiLoGo-U. Compared with the hierarchical graph network CAtt-BiUGNN, BiLoGo-T reduces mean positional error by 15.5% on the Corner case and BiLoGo-U by 8.3% on the Corner+Rib case, with 66-69% less training memory.
papers.title_ja: BiLoGo: シート成形におけるTransformerベースのニューラルオペレータによる局所応答の平滑化低減
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、シート成形の有限要素法（FE）シミュレーションを高速化しつつ、リブ周辺などの局所的な肉厚変化を正確に捉えるための学習型シミュレータ「BiLoGo」を提案する。局所的なノード-要素間の情報伝達を行うグラフSAGEモデルと、長距離依存性を扱うTransformerベースのニューラルオペレータを双方向に結合し、局所情報を全体平均で平滑化しない設計を採用した。ドーム型冷間成形やコーナー型熱間プレス成形のケーススタディにおいて、既存のグラフベースモデルや純粋なニューラルオペレータと比較し、肉厚誤差を大幅に低減するとともに、学習時のメモリ使用量も66〜69%削減した。
papers.relevance_reason: ニューラルオペレータと物理シミュレーションの高速化という関心領域に完全に一致

papers.title: ResQAdam: Residual-Preserving Adaptive Optimization for Memory-Efficient Quantization Aware Training
papers.summary: Quantization-aware training (QAT) is the most reliable way to obtain accurate low-bit large language models (LLMs), but training with AdamW keeps two dense FP32 states for every weight matrix. We find that low-rank memory-efficient optimizers such as GaLore and LDAdam degrade substantially in QAT. A considerable part of the QAT momentum lies outside its top-r singular subspace, and projection-based methods discard this part at every step. We further observe that this residual remains useful when only its sign is kept. Based on these observations, we propose ResQAdam. It keeps a single BF16 momentum, applies Adam only to the r x r coordinates of the principal subspace, and adds a normalized sign update computed from the residual. We evaluate ResQAdam with two from-scratch QAT methods and three QAT fine-tuning pipelines, with weights quantized down to 2 bits. It reduces optimizer-state memory by 71% to 74% relative to AdamW, stays close to AdamW in most settings, and lowers training throughput by less than 2%.
papers.title_ja: ResQAdam: メモリ効率の良い量子化認識学習のための残差保持型適応最適化
papers.summary_ja: 大規模言語モデル（LLM）の量子化認識学習（QAT）において、既存の低ランク最適化手法が精度を損なう問題に対し、新しい最適化アルゴリズム「ResQAdam」を提案する。本手法は、主成分部分空間に対してAdam更新を行い、残差部分に対しては符号のみを保持した正規化更新を加えることで、量子化時のモーメンタム情報を効果的に活用する。これにより、AdamWと比較してオプティマイザ状態のメモリ使用量を71〜74%削減しつつ、精度を維持し、訓練スループットの低下も2%未満に抑えることを示した。
papers.relevance_reason: LLMの量子化とメモリ効率化というユーザーの関心に直接該当する。

papers.title: Scout Before You Route: Predicting Task Success and Token Count from a Small LLM Prefill
papers.summary: Routers typically choose a model per query by trading predicted correctness against cost. Most price each model at a fixed cost, as if every query used the same number of output tokens, but the output length of reasoning models varies by an order of magnitude across queries. When is per-query cost worth predicting? What factors drive cost? How cheaply can predictions be made? We predict both the success probability and the output length of candidate models from the prefill activations of a single small frozen LLM, the scout. With reasoning candidates, perfect per-query cost knowledge would save 29-61% of spending on eight of nine datasets, and much less with non-reasoning candidates on the same problems. On those eight datasets, our predicted costs save 9-33% at matched accuracy relative to median-length pricing, up to 69% of what perfect knowledge would save. They are significantly cheaper than each estimator we reimplemented or adapted from published work, including ZeroRouter and a MixLLM-style predictor, on a majority of datasets. Output length depends mostly on the problem. On most math and code datasets, harder problems are longer, so predicted success alone prices cost nearly as well. On knowledge and mixed-format datasets they are not, and predicted success falls well behind a probe trained on length. The probe keeps most of its saving with 20 labelled problems and transfers without labels to four of seven new benchmarks. On a mixture of all nine benchmarks, it saves 22% beyond pricing each benchmark at its own median length. Savings stop growing at about a 2B scout, so above 4B a larger scout costs more than it adds.
papers.title_ja: ルーティング前にスカウトせよ：小型LLMのプリフィルからタスク成功確率とトークン数を予測する
papers.summary_ja: 推論モデルの出力長がクエリごとに大きく変動するため、固定コストでのルーティングは非効率である。本論文は、小型の凍結LLM（スカウト）のプリフィル活性化から、候補モデルの成功確率と出力トークン数を予測する手法を提案する。この予測により、精度を維持しつつ支出を9〜33%削減でき、完全なコスト知識による節約の最大69%を達成した。出力長は主に問題の難易度に依存し、知識系データセットでは長さ予測プローブが成功確率予測より優れる。2B規模のスカウトで効果が頭打ちとなり、4B以上ではコスト対効果が悪化することが示された。
papers.relevance_reason: LLM推論コスト最適化とルーティング設計の核心を扱う

papers.title: Safe Circumnavigation on Heterogeneous Orbits: A Range-Only HOCBF-QP Framework for Nonholonomic Multi-Agent Systems
papers.summary: Circumnavigating a stationary target with a team of robots requires each robot to hold its own standoff distance, to stay evenly spaced from its neighbours, and to avoid collisions with the target and with each other at every instant. The task becomes arduous when the robots are assigned different orbital radii, as their sensors or roles may demand. This paper presents a safety-critical control framework for this problem. Each robot commands both its acceleration and its turn-rate, measures only its distance to the target, and exchanges information only with its two ring neighbours. The design has three features. First, a structural property of the model lets one control law serve every robot regardless of its assigned radius. Second, the acceleration drives each radius exactly to its target, while the turn-rate balances the formation with the neighbours. Third, a higher-order control-barrier-function quadratic program enforces target, geofence, and inter-robot safety on both inputs at once; it leaves the nominal controller untouched away from the constraints and stays valid while the unmeasured range rate is still being estimated. Simulations confirm these guarantees. In a comparison, the closest existing multi-orbit design, even with full state information, violates both the target standoff and the inter-robot margin, whereas the proposed controller does not.
papers.title_ja: 非ホロノミック多エージェントシステムにおける異種軌道での安全な周回：レンジオンリーHOCBF-QPフレームワーク
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、異なる軌道半径を持つロボット群が静止ターゲットを安全に周回するための制御フレームワークを提案する。各ロボットはターゲットまでの距離のみを測定し、隣接する2つのロボットとのみ情報共有を行う。高次制御バリア関数（HOCBF）と二次計画（QP）を用いることで、ターゲット回避・地理フェンス・ロボット間衝突回避の安全性を厳密に保証しつつ、名目制御器を妨げずに動作する。シミュレーションにより、既存手法が安全制約を破るのに対し、本手法が制約を維持しつつ安定した隊形維持を実現することを示した。
papers.relevance_reason: 軌道力学と機械学習制御（QP）の組み合わせであり、ユーザーの関心領域に合致

papers.title: The dynamics through the first two Lagrange necks in the small-mass restricted three-body problem
papers.summary: We study the planar circular restricted three-body problem (PCR3BP) for sufficiently small mass ratios, from low energies to slightly above the second Lagrange value. We show that retrograde orbits around the primaries and Lyapunov orbits at the necks form the binding of a finite energy foliation. We construct these foliations using the theory of pseudoholomorphic curves in symplectizations developed by Hofer, Wysocki and Zehnder. Slightly above the second Lagrange value, the dynamics is transverse to families of disks bounded by the retrograde orbits, and cylinders connecting the retrograde orbits to the Lyapunov orbits, forming a $3-2-3-2$ foliation. The proof uses the rotating Kepler problem and Hill's lunar problem to control the singular limit as the mass ratio $\mu \to 0$. As a consequence of the foliation, both Lyapunov orbits have infinitely many homoclinic orbits.
papers.title_ja: 小質量制限三体問題における最初の2つのラグランジュネックを通るダイナミクス
papers.summary_ja: 小質量比の平面円周制限三体問題（PCR3BP）において、低エネルギーから第2ラグランジュ値のわずかに上までの軌道構造を解析した。ホーファーらによる擬正則曲線理論を用い、逆行軌道とラグランジュネック上のリアプノフ軌道が有限エネルギーの葉層構造を形成することを示した。さらに、第2ラグランジュ値を超えた領域では、これらの軌道が円盤や円筒を形成する3-2-3-2葉層構造を持つことを証明した。この結果から、両方のリアプノフ軌道が無限個のホモクリン軌道を持つことが導かれる。
papers.relevance_reason: 三体問題の軌道力学と安定性解析であり、ユーザーの関心領域に直接該当する。

papers.title: Embedding Consistent Recurrent Neural Networks in Finite Element Simulations for Path-Dependent Damage Prediction
papers.summary: Capturing sheet-metal localisation physics with a trained surrogate inside a finite element (FEM) solver requires the surrogate to deliver consistent predictions irrespective of the solver's strain-increment count, which is difficult to control in non-linear explicit codes. We address this by re-implementing a trained recurrent neural network (RNN) damage criterion in Fortran and embed it as a live, increment-by-increment fracture criterion inside an Abaqus/Explicit user material subroutine (VUMAT), advancing the network state alongside the solver. Two architectures are compared: a SimpleRNN and the proposed Consistent RNN (ConsRNN), whose transition function is designed so that predictions converge as the strain path is refined rather than drifting with the increment count. Both are trained on bilinear strain paths and evaluated under varying temporal discretisations and nonlinear histories. SimpleRNN predictions drift as the increment count increases, which disqualifies it for embedding; ConsRNN converges under refinement, at a substantial fixed-resolution accuracy cost relative to SimpleRNN on multilinear paths. Deployed at structural scale, the embedded ConsRNN surrogate governs element deletion in a clamped steel plate and reaches the same peak force and peak displacement as an established two-parameter fracture criterion. This pre-peak agreement is expected by construction, since no element is deleted before the peak and the two runs therefore share an identical constitutive path; the responses diverge only on the post-peak softening branch. The results establish discretisation consistency as the decisive property for embedding recurrent surrogates in explicit FEM solvers, and report the first embedding of a customised, non-standard-transition recurrent cell at structural scale.
papers.title_ja: 有限要素法シミュレーションへの埋め込みによる経路依存性損傷予測のための埋め込み整合性再帰ニューラルネットワーク
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、有限要素法（FEM）ソルバー内で使用可能な経路依存性損傷予測のためのサロゲートモデルとして、再帰ニューラルネットワーク（RNN）の埋め込み手法を提案する。既存のSimpleRNNは時間離散化（増分数）に依存して予測がドリフトする問題があるため、増分数を細かくしても予測が収束するよう設計されたConsistent RNN（ConsRNN）を開発した。Abaqus/ExplicitのVUMATサブプログラム内にFortranで実装し、要素削除基準として構造スケールで適用した結果、確立された破壊基準と同等のピーク荷重・変位を再現した。本研究は、明示的FEMソルバーへのRNNサロゲートの埋め込みにおいて、離散化整合性が決定的な要件であることを示し、非標準遷移関数を持つRNNセルの構造スケールへの初回埋め込みを報告している。
papers.relevance_reason: サロゲートモデルと物理シミュレーション（FEM）の統合という関心に強く該当

papers.title: Interpretable Multifidelity Learning with Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for Spatiotemporal Nuclear Reactor Flow Modeling
papers.summary: High-fidelity computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations of nuclear reactor systems are computationally expensive, motivating machine learning methods that reduce cost while preserving accuracy. Multifidelity surrogate modeling addresses this by combining inexpensive low-fidelity data with limited high-fidelity data. This work investigates whether the high-fidelity data required to predict the spatiotemporal mass flow rate across all 193 fuel assemblies of a pressurized water reactor (PWR) core can be reduced, comparing black-box multifidelity feedforward neural networks (MFNNs) with interpretable multifidelity Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (MFKANs). Cross-fidelity correlation across the core is weak, making this a challenging multifidelity problem, and neither architecture predicts the transient particularly well in absolute terms. MFKAN nonetheless performs comparably to MFNN for one-time-step-forward prediction while also providing closed-form symbolic equations unavailable with MFNN. To address the scarcity of CFD transients, with only one available per fidelity level, TabDDPM-generated synthetic data was used to augment cross-fidelity forecasting. KAN and FNN achieve comparable self-evaluation accuracy (Pearson correlation of roughly 0.73--0.81), but both perform poorly at true cross-fidelity forecasting (correlations of 0.03--0.06). Assembly-level analysis shows that each assembly's forecast correlation tracks its real cross-fidelity correlation for both architectures ($r=0.840$--$0.896$ for KAN, $r=0.804$--$0.903$ for FNN), confirming that forecasting accuracy is fundamentally limited by how correlated the fidelity levels already are. Overall, KAN-based multifidelity modeling achieves accuracy consistently comparable to MFNN across all settings, while additionally providing symbolic equations that match or exceed the spline representation's accuracy.

papers.title: Minimum-Sufficient Knowledge and Computation for Wind Energy Predictive Analysis
papers.summary: Resource-constrained cyber-physical decision systems often apply fixed sensing, knowledge, and computational pipelines despite state-dependent information needs. We introduce Minimum-Sufficient Knowledge and Computation (MSKC), a resource-aware computing principle: select the least-costly route meeting decision-risk and deployment constraints, escalating only when cheaper routes are insufficient. As proof of concept, we isolate adaptive knowledge routing, the decision underlying Knowledge-Guided Machine Learning (KGML), which conventionally injects external knowledge unconditionally rather than only where needed. We instantiate this for wind ramp-event predictive analysis, an edge-oriented decision-support task, evaluating local, relational, and physics-informed routes with a state-aware gate on publicly available real data from two wind farms. We establish conditions for feasibility preservation, cost dominance, and strict expected savings over always-on routing. At a 35.9% relational-knowledge injection rate, adaptive routing is statistically indistinguishable from always-on injection on the reported metrics while reducing knowledge calls by 64%, supporting sustainable, Green-IT-aligned deployment. These results support MSKC's premise that uniformly maximal intelligence is unnecessary. This offers intelligent data analysis for big data streams: the analysis itself decides, per state, how much knowledge and computation the data warrant.
papers.title_ja: 風力発電予測分析における最小十分知識と計算

papers.title: Solver-Admitted Metamorphic Testing of Learned Network Optimization Surrogates
papers.summary: Equivalent encodings of an optimization problem can produce different learned predictions. Interpreting these differences requires accounting for numerical error and multiple optima. We construct metamorphic tests for optimization solver surrogates with explicit eligibility conditions, output alignment, and numerical thresholds. Reference-solver agreement and independent constraint checks determine which sampled pairs enter the audit. We study alternating-current optimal power flow (AC-OPF), the traveling salesman problem (TSP), the capacitated vehicle routing problem (CVRP), and maximum independent set (MIS). Across five grids, GridSFM-Open violates each of 13 relations on at least one grid, and 12 by more than twice the threshold. Randomly initialized copies of the grid models fail nearly the same relations, so the failures do not require training. Source patches and input canonicalization remove selected discrepancies, but no intervention establishes preserved accuracy and feasibility within the declared margin on every grid. In routing, Policy Optimization with Multiple Optima (POMO) has a single-pass rotation/reflection violation rate that rises from 12.7% to 89.5% between 20 and 100 cities. Graph-Based Diffusion Solvers for Combinatorial Optimization (DIFUSCO) violates the MIS disjoint-union relation on 35.6% of draws. Post hoc normalization within connected components removes these violations on the tested graphs. These findings support reporting metamorphic consistency alongside optimality, feasibility, and accuracy, and validating repair quality separately from consistency.
papers.title_ja: 学習されたネットワーク最適化サロゲートのソルバー承認メタモルフィックテスト
papers.summary_ja: 最適化問題のサロゲートモデルにおける予測の不一致を、数値誤差や多重最適解を考慮したメタモルフィックテストで評価する手法を提案する。AC-OPF、TSP、CVRP、MISなどの問題で検証し、既存モデルが多くの関係性を満たさないことを示した。特にルーティング問題では、都市数増加に伴い回転・対称性に関する違反率が急上昇することが判明した。これらの結果は、最適性や実現可能性に加え、メタモルフィック一貫性の報告と検証の重要性を支持するものである。

papers.title: Learning to Restart: Differentiable Restart Policies for Optimization Dynamics
papers.summary: Adaptive restart mechanisms, which reset the momentum or other auxiliary state of an iterative optimizer, play a central role in the empirical performance of accelerated first-order methods, yet existing restart rules remain almost entirely hand-designed. The obstruction to learning restart policies is that, unlike the typical Learning to Optimize (L2O) setting, the discrete restart events make the resulting trajectory non-differentiable in the algorithm parameters and thus block gradient-based optimization of the restart policy. We resolve this obstruction by developing a differentiable framework for restart policies through their continuous-time limit. We introduce surrogate gradients for the restart events and optimization trajectories that are efficient to compute and provably converge to their continuous-time counterparts. We validate the effectiveness of our surrogate gradients in L2O settings, training restart policies that improve upon standard handcrafted adaptive restart criteria on quadratic and linear programs, and that transfer zero-shot from synthetic quadratics to logistic regression on real datasets.
papers.title_ja: 再スタートを学ぶ：最適化ダイナミクスにおける微分可能な再スタートポリシー

papers.title: Surrogate Quality Score: A Novel Composite Performance Metric for Model Selection
papers.summary: The growing reliance on high-fidelity, state-of-the-art machine learning based models for engineering decision-making necessitates robust and systematic approaches for model selection. While high predictive accuracy at untrained points is a necessary trait in the final model, other attributes such as model complexity, forecastability, explainability, scalability, and physics-awareness may be equally important or relevant criteria depending on application context and user requirements. In this work, we propose a novel composite performance metric, Surrogate Quality Score (SQS) for model selection based on predictive accuracy and model complexity simultaneously. SQS heuristically integrates these two attributes through a weighted product of normalized measures, yielding a unified score to reflect overall model quality. A user-specified parameter in SQS enables explicit control over the accuracy-complexity trade-off, thereby incorporating human judgement and preference in the model selection process. We extensively discuss and justify the formulation of SQS and demonstrate its utility through an illustrative example. By combining predictive accuracy and model complexity, SQS offers a systematic and objective approach for model selection based on both attributes.
papers.title_ja: サロゲート品質スコア：モデル選択のための新しい複合性能指標

papers.title: Stable probabilistic emulation of partially observed dynamical systems
papers.summary: Predicting the long-term behavior of partially observed dynamical systems such as the coupled atmosphere-ocean system is central to societal decision-making. Motivated by the success of deep learning emulators in weather forecasting, data-driven climate models represent a promising approach. However, climate emulation poses distinct challenges: models must account for unresolved fast variables introduced by unavoidable coarse-graining, reproduce long-term statistics, and remain stable over arbitrarily long rollouts and under external perturbations. These requirements motivate stochastic data-driven emulators, but modern generative models lack stability guarantees. We introduce forced-dissipative stochastic interpolants, a generative framework for learning stochastic reduced dynamics. Its architecture uses structural constraints inspired by turbulent dynamics, which provide stability by design while retaining the flexibility of stochastic interpolants to represent complex probabilistic dynamics. Building on the theory of Markov-chain stability, we establish a Foster--Lyapunov drift condition and prove geometric ergodicity for our emulator, together with stability under steady external forcing. We evaluate the framework on the two-timescale Lorenz-96 system, a prototype of partially observed multiscale turbulence. The resulting emulator remains stable over long integrations and under finite-amplitude forcing, with accurate prediction of forced responses of both the mean and variance.
papers.title_ja: 部分観測動力学系の安定確率エミュレーション

papers.title: A scaled TW-PINN framework for soliton solutions of the Korteweg--de Vries equation
papers.summary: Accurate approximation of soliton solutions of the Korteweg--de Vries (KdV) equation remains challenging for physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) due to localized wave structures, high-order spatial derivatives, nonlinear interactions between solitons, and difficulties in long-time prediction. In this work, we address these challenges using a scaling PINN framework to approximate KdV soliton solutions. The framework transforms the governing equation into a normalized form, approximates its solution using a PINN solver, and reconstructs the solution in the original variables through inverse scaling. We introduce scaling transformations and PINN solvers tailored to one- and two-soliton problems. For the one-soliton case, we employ a PINN solver that incorporates a traveling-wave coordinate to capture soliton propagation. For the two-soliton case, we employ a two-step training procedure for the PINN solver. The first step learns the individual soliton profiles and estimates their propagation speeds, while the second step uses the estimated speeds to construct traveling-wave coordinates in the PINN solver and approximate the full two-soliton solution, including nonlinear interactions. We also introduce soliton-informed sampling (SIS), which places additional collocation points around the soliton trajectories. Numerical results show that the scaling PINN framework accurately captures one-soliton propagation, resolves two-soliton interactions, and preserves soliton profiles during long-time extrapolation in both cases. An additional three-soliton experiment suggests the applicability of the proposed two-step training procedure to multi-soliton solutions.
papers.title_ja: コルテウェーグ・ド・フリース方程式のソリトン解のためのスケーリングTW-PINNフレームワーク

papers.title: EDP-PI-DOSnet: An Energy Dissipation Preserving Neural Solver for Two-Phase Flow Problems
papers.summary: Preserving the energy dissipation properties of gradient flow equations is important for the stability and reliability of numerical approximations, particularly in long-time simulations. In this paper, we propose a class of energy-dissipation-preserving physics-informed deep operator splitting networks (EDP-PI-DOSnets) for solving gradient flow equations. The proposed framework incorporates classical structure-preserving numerical schemes into neural network architectures, allowing the corresponding discrete energy dissipation laws to be preserved. In particular, suitable constraints are imposed on the convolution kernels to ensure that the learned discrete operators are symmetric and negative semidefinite. Furthermore, several network formulations are developed based on the Crank--Nicolson (CN), scalar auxiliary variable Crank--Nicolson (SAV/CN), and relaxed discrete variational derivative (R-DVD-1) schemes. Meanwhile, a physics-informed loss function based on the residuals of the governing equations is employed. Numerical experiments show that the predicted solutions are in good agreement with the reference solutions while satisfying the corresponding discrete energy dissipation laws. The results also suggest stable behavior during long-time recursive prediction and the potential applicability of the proposed framework to two-phase flow problems.
papers.title_ja: EDP-PI-DOSnet: 二相流問題のためのエネルギー散逸保存型ニューラルソルバ

papers.title: StockASkill: A Local-First AgentSkill for Intelligent Stock Selection
papers.summary: Quantitative equity selection and portfolio construction in emerging and cross-border markets frequently suffer from computational bottlenecks, remote API fragility, survivorship bias, and rigid execution constraints such as discrete board lots and investor-mandated drawdown limits. In this paper, we present StockASkill, a local-first, full-data-driven AgentSkill engineered as a specialized Quant Co-Processor for autonomous AI agents and quantitative researchers. Tailored for agile portfolios (10^5 ~ 10^7 RMB) where discrete lot execution and capital protection are mandatory, StockASkill embeds a columnar DuckDB OLAP engine over 42.44 million historical price records and 186,432 financial disclosures spanning 26 years across China A-shares, Hong Kong, US equities, and ETFs. By eliminating ad-hoc network dependencies during analysis, StockASkill reduces cross-sectional screening latency across 5,400+ equities from over 25 seconds to sub-0.5 seconds (a 95%+ reduction). We formalize an end-to-end mathematical pipeline integrating a 7+1 factor alpha model, an SLSQP convex optimizer under smooth CVaR drawdown surrogates with exact path projection, dynamic 100-share board lot integer quantization, and an autonomous thesis lifecycle finite-state machine. Furthermore, we provide a zero-disk, strongly-typed JSON streaming interface designed for high-throughput LLM tool-calling. Open-sourced at https://github.com/axjing/stockaskill, comprehensive empirical benchmarks from 2018 to 2024 demonstrate that the architecture achieves annualized Sharpe ratios exceeding 1.48 and Calmar ratios up to 2.17, while reducing max drawdown by up to 85% relative to benchmark indices.

papers.title: TurtLES: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Turbulent 3D Neural PDE Surrogates
papers.summary: Machine-learning surrogates are increasingly used to accelerate computational fluid dynamics, yet progress is limited by the lack of benchmarks capturing realistic, time-dependent turbulent flows. We introduce TurtLES, a 14 TB dataset of 3D turbulent cylinder wakes in the shear-layer transition regime, computed via high-fidelity implicit large-eddy simulations. The dataset contains 400 trajectories of 400 time steps each, with 3-11 million points per frame, spanning variations in geometry, Reynolds number, and angle of attack. Unlike existing datasets, TurtLES combines (i) physically realistic turbulence with an active energy cascade driven by vortex stretching, (ii) dense irregular meshes, and (iii) long-horizon temporal dynamics. We benchmark state-of-the-art neural operators on autoregressive rollouts and identify key failure modes, including temporal instability, loss of small-scale energy, and challenges in learning on large irregular domains. TurtLES provides a new benchmark for evaluating surrogate models on 3D turbulent wakes at industrially relevant mesh resolution.

papers.title: FoundaRF: A Physics-Informed Foundation Model Framework for Radio-Frequency Passive Components
papers.summary: Designing RF/mmWave passive components is a time-consuming process that relies heavily on expert knowledge and iterative EM simulations. Although recent ML surrogate models have shown great promise in accelerating passive design, they remain task-specific and lack generalization. This paper presents FoundaRF, a foundation model framework that unifies passive layout modeling across diverse layout structures and technologies. It combines a self-supervised encoder with adaptive layout processing and physics-aware decoders to enable few-shot transfer. Experiments across four semiconductor technologies show strong generalization to unseen structures, outperforming baselines with up to a 3.3x reduction in prediction error, reducing labeled-data requirements by up to fourfold, and substantially shortening design turnaround. FoundaRF establishes a scalable and data-efficient solution for RF/mmWave passive design automation.

papers.title: DrivAerRim: A large-scale full-vehicle CFD dataset for wheel rim aerodynamics
papers.summary: The wheel region contributes substantially to vehicle aerodynamic drag, and rim geometry strongly influences the flow in this region. However, publicly available automotive aerodynamics datasets offer limited variation in rim design. We present DrivAerRim, a large-scale dataset of full-vehicle computational fluid dynamics simulations covering 904 DeepWheel rim designs with diverse spoke layouts, opening areas and topologies. All cases use the same DrivAer Estateback, operating conditions and numerical setup, with rim geometry as the sole design variable. Wheel rotation is modelled using moving reference frame regions around the rims and rotating wall conditions on the deformed tyres. The numerical setup is assessed through mesh sensitivity analysis and comparisons with wind tunnel measurements. The resulting 9.32 TB release includes wheel geometries, vehicle and component force coefficients, accumulated drag, surface pressure, wall shear stress, and flow fields around the vehicle and wheels. Together, these data support surrogate model training and evaluation across diverse rim geometries, as well as aerodynamic optimisation and generative design to accelerate wheel rim development for vehicle drag reduction.
papers.title_ja: DrivAerRim: ホイールリム空力特性のための大規模フルビークルCFDデータセット

papers.title: A Structured-Surrogate Double-Model Approach to Regularization Parameter Selection
papers.summary: Double-model methods select a regularization parameter by matching the discrepancy between two reconstructions of the same data to a prescribed target. The Structured-Surrogate Double-Model (SSDM) framework is developed around a computationally inexpensive structured surrogate of the forward operator and a spectrally explicit perturbation, with the selected parameter subsequently applied to the original inverse problem. Given a prescribed target, parameter selection requires neither prior knowledge of the noise level nor training data. For a class of Tikhonov regularization problems, the squared discrepancy is shown to attain a strict maximum at zero regularization, decay as $\lambda^{-2}$, and decrease strictly beyond an explicit phase-aware threshold. A complementary, data-dependent certificate is established to guarantee strict monotonicity on finite intervals, enabling unique and reliable target matching even when the global threshold is overly conservative. The discrepancy is further connected to directional roughness in image deblurring, providing a geometric interpretation of the selection principle. Experiments on synthetic images and on synthetically blurred natural photographs illustrate the theoretical findings and demonstrate the practical applicability of certified parameter selection.
papers.title_ja: 正則化パラメータ選択のための構造化サロゲート・ダブルモデルアプローチ
papers.summary_ja: 逆問題における正則化パラメータ選択を高速化するため、前進演算子の構造化サロゲートモデルを用いたSSDMフレームワークを提案する。この手法は、ノイズレベルの事前知識や学習データなしで、2つの再構成解の乖離を目標値に一致させることでパラメータを決定する。Tikhonov正則化問題において、乖離が正則化パラメータに対して厳密に単調減少することを理論的に証明し、一意かつ信頼性の高い選択を保証する。画像ぼけ除去の合成データおよび自然写真を用いた実験により、理論的有効性と実用性を示した。

papers.title: A Physics-Informed Learning Framework for Linking Microscopic Surface Degradation to Bolted Joint Functional Behavior
papers.summary: Returned products in circular engineering often have heterogeneous degradation histories, making remaining function difficult to assess. For bolted joints, corrosion alters surface morphology, contact, friction, preload retention, and mechanical response. This paper presents a physics-informed multimodal framework for linking microscopic and camera-based degradation observations to functional indicators of corroded bolted joints. The workflow defines the corrosion failure mode, generates synchronized inspection and functional-response records, preprocesses image, roughness, exposure, and joint descriptors, aligns microscopy and camera observations through similarity learning, and constructs a calibrated corrosion-severity field. Partial differential equation (PDE) discovery is applied to this field to identify candidate effective mesoscale laws rather than complete electrochemical mechanisms. The corrosion-evolution model is coupled to a separate functional model, with friction coefficient as the primary target and preload loss included when clamp-force data are available. The contribution is a reproducible pathway for physically constrained assessment of degraded bolted-joint behavior.
papers.title_ja: ボルト接合部の微小表面劣化と機能特性を関連付ける物理情報学習フレームワーク
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、腐食したボルト接合部の微小な表面劣化観察と機能指標を結びつける物理情報マルチモーダルフレームワークを提案する。類似度学習による画像整合とPDE発見手法を用いて、完全な電気化学機構ではなく有効なメソスケールの法則を特定する。この腐食進化モデルは摩擦係数や予張力損失をターゲットとする機能モデルと結合され、物理的に制約された劣化評価の再現可能な経路を提供する。

papers.title: Turbulent wakes behind nine bluff-body shapes from direct numerical simulation and particle image velocimetry
papers.summary: We present a cross-validated dataset of turbulent wakes behind nine bluff bodies at Reynolds number Re = 10,000: a circular cylinder, a 2:1 elliptical cylinder at 0{\deg} and 90{\deg}, short and long isosceles triangles with the apex upstream or downstream, and a square cylinder at 0{\deg} and 45{\deg}. Each body was studied by wall-resolved direct numerical simulation (DNS) with a spectral-element solver and by time-resolved planar particle image velocimetry (PIV) in the MIT Intelligent Towing Tank. The DNS records contain time- and spanwise-averaged velocity, pressure and Reynolds stresses, 24-bin phase-averaged fields keyed to the lift signal, drag and lift histories, and one three-dimensional instantaneous snapshot per body; the PIV records contain the matching time-mean and phase-averaged fields in the same coordinate frame. The DNS set-up is verified against reference cylinder data at Re = 3900, and DNS and PIV at Re = 10,000 are compared field by field. The dataset supports the development and testing of data-driven turbulence closures, reduced-order models, and wake-stability analyses across geometries with distinct separation behavior.
papers.title_ja: 直接数値シミュレーションと粒子画像速度計測による9種類の鈍体形状の乱流尾流
papers.summary_ja: レイノルズ数10,000における9種類の鈍体形状の乱流尾流について、直接数値シミュレーション（DNS）と粒子画像速度計測（PIV）による相互検証済みデータセットを公開する。DNSはスペクトル要素法を用いた壁面解像計算であり、時間平均・位相平均速度場、圧力、レイノルズ応力、および3次元瞬間スナップショットを含む。PIVデータは同一座標系での対応する平均場を提供し、両者はフィールド単位で比較検証されている。本データセットは、データ駆動型乱流閉鎖則、縮約モデル（ROM）、および尾流安定性解析の開発とテストを支援することを目的としている。

papers.title: Rethinking Data Selection as Distribution Matching on Semantic Manifolds
papers.summary: Instruction tuning of large language models and large vision language models relies on massive training data, which incurs substantial computational and storage costs. Meanwhile, training data often contains redundancy, noise, and low quality samples. Existing data selection methods mostly rely on diversity, importance, or a combination of both, without explicitly constraining the distributional consistency between the selected subset and the full data in the embedding space. We propose QMAC, a quality aware multiband characteristic function matching method that formulates data selection as a joint optimization problem of distribution matching and quality filtering. QMAC matches the empirical characteristic functions of the selected subset and the full data across multiple frequency scales, capturing both global semantic coverage and local perturbations, while using task related quality scores to filter noisy and low quality samples. We systematically evaluate QMAC on 4 data types, 8 target models, and 44 benchmarks. Experimental results show that QMAC outperforms existing data selection baselines on standard image-text instruction data, substantially surpasses random selection on standard text instruction, image-text reasoning, and text reasoning data, and exceeds full data training in multiple model and budget combinations. The code will be made publicly available upon acceptance of the paper.
papers.title_ja: 意味多様体上の分布マッチングとしてのデータ選択の再考
papers.summary_ja: 大規模言語モデルのインストラクションチューニングにおけるデータ選択手法として、QMAC（品質認識マルチバンド特性関数マッチング）を提案する。本手法は、選択済みサブセットと全データ間の分布整合性を明示的に制約し、多周波数スケールでの特性関数マッチングとタスク関連の品質スコアによるフィルタリングを統合した最適化問題として定式化する。44種のベンチマークでの評価により、既存手法やランダム選択を上回り、場合によっては全データ学習を超える性能を示した。

papers.title: Emergent Low-Dimensional Topological Dynamics Dictate Generalization and Escape Mechanics in Billion-Parameter Neural Networks
papers.summary: The remarkable generalization of modern over-parameterized neural networks defies classical statistical learning bounds. Here we establish that optimization trajectories in billion-parameter models do not sample the ambient dimension $\mathbb{R}^N$ homogeneously; instead, they are dynamically constrained to a low-dimensional execution submanifold $\mathcal{M}_{\text{exec}}$ (with empirically observed effective dimension $d_{\text{eff}} \le 12$). By equipping the parameter space with a regularized Hessian metric $g_{ij} = \nabla_i \nabla_j L + \epsilon \delta_{ij}$ and analyzing stochastic Langevin diffusion on loss sublevel sets, we derive a rigorous Topological Generalization Bound grounded in projected subspace persistent homology. Furthermore, by linking Morse index transitions to Betti number annihilation ($\beta_1 \to 0$), we formulate an exact mathematical mechanism for exponential escape from strict saddles under anisotropic noise. We validate our framework across 80+ architectures (ResNets, Vision Transformers, and 7B LLMs). To bridge theoretical topology with computational feasibility, we resolve the curse of dimensionality by computing projected persistent homology proxies via randomized Lanczos iterations restricted strictly within active Hessian subspaces. Building upon this mathematical foundation, we introduce Topological-Adaptive Optimization (Top-SGD and Top-AdamW)---a family of wrapper algorithms that dynamically modulate learning rates using active curvature signatures. Extensive benchmarks demonstrate a 14.1\% reduction in total wall-clock training time on ImageNet with all computational and memory overheads fully accounted for. Code is publicly available at https://github.com/imslab-research/Topological-SGD.
papers.title_ja: 十億パラメータニューラルネットワークにおける汎化と脱出メカニズムを規定する創発的低次元トポロジカルダイナミクス
papers.summary_ja: 本研究では、大規模ニューラルネットワークの最適化軌道が低次元部分多様体に制約されることを示し、正則化ヘッセ行列計量を用いたトポロジカル汎化境界を導出する。モーセ指数遷移とベッティ数の消滅を関連付けることで、厳密なサドル点からの脱出メカニズムを数学的に定式化し、ランダム化ランコス反復により計算コストを低減する手法を提案する。さらに、アクティブ曲率シグネチャに基づいて学習率を動的調整するTop-SGDやTop-AdamWを実装し、ImageNetでの訓練時間を14.1%短縮する成果を実証した。

papers.title: What Are LLM Agents Actually Learning on Low-Budget Molecular Optimization Benchmarks?
papers.summary: Recent work reports large gains for LLM agents on low-budget molecular optimization. We measure the contributions of online optimization, retrievable task information, and permissive oracle landscapes. On PMO at 50 oracle calls, a GPT-4o mini agent's sum AUC falls from 14.44 to 4.85 after task names and curated reference compounds are hidden. An identity-blinded condition that states only the oracle form (e.g., similarity to a hidden reference) scores 5.39, while a deterministic retrieval-only baseline with no LLM reaches 12.16 (84% of the full agent). A full 23-task 2x2 ablation and a three-seed replication on eight tasks support this interpretation. On a protein-targeted benchmark with an AutoDock Vina composite oracle, a single-edit random walk is a strong lower bound; across three seeds it obtains composite 0.636 +/- 0.008 and docking improvement -1.11 +/- 0.04 kcal/mol. As a positive control, a retrieval-free population agent exceeds REINVENT at a matched 50-call AUC budget, with its strongest result at 100 calls. These results motivate two inexpensive sanity checks: retrieval-safe PMO prompts and a random-walk floor for docking-based optimization.
papers.title_ja: 低予算分子最適化ベンチマークにおいてLLMエージェントは実際に何を学習しているのか？
papers.summary_ja: 低予算分子最適化におけるLLMエージェントの性能向上要因を分析し、オンライン最適化や検索可能なタスク情報、寛容なオラクル景観の寄与を定量化した。タスク名や参照化合物を隠蔽すると性能が大幅に低下し、LLMを使わない決定論的な検索ベースラインが同等以上の結果を出すことを示した。さらに、タンパク質標的ベンチマークではランダムウォークが強力な下限基準となり、検索なしの集団エージェントがREINVENTを上回ることを確認した。これらの結果から、検索安全なプロンプト設計とランダムウォークによる妥当性チェックの重要性を提言している。
papers.relevance_reason: LLMエージェント設計とRAG、評価手法・ベンチマークの検証に直結する

papers.title: How Small Can We Go? Calibrating Activation-Cache Compression for SAE Training
papers.summary: To train a sparse autoencoder (SAE), you need a massive cache of model activations. We look into the effects that compression has on an SAE in two ways: we keep the original fp32-trained SAE and pass the compressed cache into the same SAE to see how many feature activations stay the same (the frozen-SAE test), and we retrain an SAE on the compressed cache and see how many of the original features still exist (the retraining test). We found that in the retraining test, there is no clear scale for retained features. On a GPT-2 cache, rounding everything to fp16 keeps 60.6% of features, but changing one value in a million by the smallest step fp32 allows (a change eight orders of magnitude smaller) keeps only 70.5%. Meanwhile, changing the random seed keeps 23.0%. For the frozen-SAE test, the frozen SAE's correlation with the original increases in order of how precise the codecs are, but plain $L_2$ distance gives nearly the same ordering. We also see the same frozen reading correspond to different percentages retained at different sites. This leaves the question of the right measurement. We build one by calibrating: retraining on identical bytes sets the ceiling, and a reseed sets the floor. We then measure the effect of each compressed codec against its own site's floor. With TopK SAEs on GPT-2 small and Pythia-1.4B at research-scale budgets, na\"ive per-token int4 loses more features than a reseed everywhere we tested, as do PCA and random projection on GPT-2. Standardizing each channel before quantizing brings int4 back above the floor in terms of retained features, at the same raw file size. At our smallest budget, a bf16 forward pass, which some pipelines use to save memory, loses slightly more features than rotated 8-bit storage. Calibrating a site costs four training runs and two evaluation passes.
papers.title_ja: どこまで小さくできるか？SAE学習における活性化キャッシュ圧縮の較正
papers.summary_ja: スパースオートエンコーダ（SAE）の学習に必要な大規模な活性化キャッシュの圧縮が、特徴量保持率に与える影響を評価する手法を提案する。既存のSAEに圧縮キャッシュを入力する「凍結SAEテスト」と、圧縮キャッシュで再学習する「再学習テスト」の2つの視点から分析した。その結果、単純なint4量子化やPCAはランダムシード変更による劣化よりも特徴量を大きく失うことが判明した。一方、チャネルごとの標準化を施したint4量子化は、同じファイルサイズで特徴量保持率を向上させることを示した。さらに、サイトごとの基準（フロア）を較正することで、圧縮手法の効果をより正確に比較できる評価フレームワークを構築した。
papers.relevance_reason: LLMの量子化・効率化と解釈可能性（SAE）の両方に深く関連する実用的な研究

papers.title: Forcing a Letter Suppresses Refusal: Mechanistic Evidence from WMDP
papers.summary: Safety benchmarks for large language models (LLMs) commonly use multiple-choice question (MCQ) format. However, prior studies documented that MCQ format reduces refusal rates, which may significantly affect the safety behavior of the model. We provide a first mechanistic explanation of this effect on the Weapons of Mass Destruction Proxy (WMDP) dataset across two models - Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen3-8B. First, we use the tuned lens technique to show that when processing MCQ the model commits to an answer-letter token very quickly, which is in contrast to the gradual refusal build-up in open-ended formats. Additionally, we observe that activations on the MCQ format lie roughly 3x further from the refusal direction, compared with their open-ended counterparts. Moreover, ablating the attention heads that carry the MCQ format answer increases the refusal, which is a direct evidence that the MCQ answer-selection competes with refusal. These findings indicate that MCQ safety scores primarily measure knowledge capabilities and do not assess the safety-mechanisms.
papers.title_ja: 文字を強制すると拒否が抑制される：WMDPからの機構的証拠
papers.summary_ja: 大規模言語モデル（LLM）の安全性評価において、選択式問題（MCQ）形式が拒否率を低下させる現象の機構的説明を行う。Tuned Lens技術を用いた解析により、MCQ処理時にモデルが早期に回答文字トークンへコミットし、オープンエンド形式のような段階的な拒否の構築が行われないことを示した。さらに、MCQ形式の活性化は拒否方向から約3倍遠く、MCQ回答を担うアテンションヘッドのアブレーションにより拒否が増加することから、回答選択と拒否が競合していることを実証した。これらの発見は、MCQによる安全性スコアが主に知識能力を測定しており、安全性メカニズムそのものを評価していないことを示唆している。
papers.relevance_reason: LLMの安全性評価手法とハルシネーション対策に直結する重要な知見

papers.title: Dual-Stream LLM-Guided Reward Design for Reject-Inference-Aware Reinforcement Learning in E-Commerce Payment Fraud Detection
papers.summary: Production fraud-detection models learn from a censored slice of their own traffic: transactions a legacy system blocked never receive fraud labels, so models train on a biased, approved-only distribution. We extend LLM-guided reward design, the framework of Qu et al. (2025) in which an LLM evolves the reward of a two-step REINFORCE fraud-blocking policy, to attack this reject-inference problem inside the reward. A single LLM designs a dual-stream reward: stream 1 applies the standard dollar-weighted precision objective to labeled transactions; stream 2 scores legacy-blocked, unlabeled transactions by contrasting the newest gradient-boosted risk signal against the legacy scores that drove the original block. Rather than prescribe which signals matter, we expose a superset of evidence and let the LLM decide for itself which to use, guided by evaluation feedback alone; because it writes the reward as code, that choice is directly auditable. On a held-out four-month out-of-time test, the dual-stream agent beats the prior labeled-only agent at every target recall, by +4.7, +2.4 and +3.0 points of dollar-weighted precision at 80%, 85% and 90% recall, and the production baseline by +6.8 points on average. The resulting policy is architecturally identical to that of Qu et al. (2025) and adds no inference cost.
papers.title_ja: EC決済不正検出における拒否推論対応強化学習のための、LLM主導のデュアルストリーム報酬設計
papers.summary_ja: EC決済の不正検出において、既存システムがブロックした取引にはラベルが付与されないという「拒否推論」問題に対し、LLMが報酬関数をコードとして設計する手法を拡張した。LLMは、ラベル付き取引に対する標準的な精度目標と、ラベル未付与のブロック済み取引に対する新旧リスクシグナルの対比評価という2つのストリームからなる報酬を自律的に設計する。このアプローチにより、評価フィードバックのみを基にLLMが最適なシグナルを選択し、監査可能な報酬関数を生成する。4ヶ月間のアウトオブタイムテストにおいて、従来のラベルのみを用いた手法や本番環境のベースラインと比較し、全リコール目標でドル加重精度を大幅に向上させた。
papers.relevance_reason: LLMと強化学習の融合、報酬設計の自動化、実務向け評価手法が含まれるため

papers.title: Patching the Blind Spots: Reversible LLM Rule Overlay for Frozen Fraud Detectors
papers.summary: In industrial tabular fraud classification, gradient-boosted trees remain state-of-the-art, but even a well-trained model has blind spots, and retraining the deployed model is not always safe. We propose a framework that patches such a model without modifying it: LLMs propose rules anchored on features the model underweights by SHAP, and the resulting noisy pool is screened for empirical support and calibrated into an additive, reversible log-lift overlay that runs at the production cut-off. Single-LLM benefit is high-variance and inverts between datasets, so we pool three diverse backbones by equal-weight logit averaging, trading peak gain for a bounded worst case. On a real-world e-commerce fraud detector trained on selection-biased data, continued training regresses even when carefully tuned, whereas the overlay gains on average +2.26% recall at equal precision ($\Delta$R@P) and +1.60% precision at equal recall ($\Delta$P@R) over production cut-offs spanning 30-57% precision and 23-63% recall. On a public benchmark of seven designed bias-shift variants it raises $\Delta$P@R on every variant and keeps $\Delta$R@P near neutral. Each amendment is a readable predicate naming the fraud pattern it covers.
papers.title_ja: 盲点を補完する：凍結済み不正検出器のための可逆的LLMルールオーバーレイ
papers.summary_ja: 産業用テーブルデータ不正分類において、再学習が困難な既存モデルの盲点をLLMで補完するフレームワークを提案する。SHAP値に基づきモデルが過小評価している特徴量にアンカーされたルールをLLMが生成し、それらをプールして加算型の可逆ログリフトオーバーレイとして実装する。単一LLMでは変動が大きいため、3つの異なるバックボーンを等重みで平均化し、最悪ケースを有界に抑える。実世界のEC不正検出器では、継続学習が性能を劣化させる一方で、本手法は同等の精度でリコールを平均+2.26%向上させ、各修正が読み取り可能な予測子として解釈可能であることを示した。
papers.relevance_reason: LLM活用と実務向け評価手法の組み合わせが関心に合致

papers.title: Jacobian-Causal Memory Control for Persistent Memory in Language Model Systems
papers.summary: Persistent-memory systems choose not only which records are retrieved but which prior information can alter current inference. We propose Jacobian-causal memory control (JCMC), which represents each authorized memory intervention by a predicted influence signature in a shared behavioral measurement space, selects interventions against a target effect and side-effect budget, and compares predicted with observed effects before retaining or rolling back the intervention. Under explicit smoothness and bounded-estimation assumptions, we prove a quadratic local-approximation bound, characterize the target effects reachable by a set of signatures, bound selection regret under signature error, and bound non-additive interactions between simultaneous memories. The paper reports no benchmark measurements; it defines a paired counterfactual estimator and an evaluation protocol comparing JCMC with relevance, graph, and policy-filtered retrieval baselines. The central claim is narrowed or falsified if those simpler baselines match effect targeting, side-effect control, and rollback utility under equal model, memory, policy, and cost budgets.
papers.title_ja: 言語モデルシステムにおける永続メモリのためのヤコビアン因果メモリ制御
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、LLMの永続メモリシステムにおいて、どの過去の情報が現在の推論に影響を与えるかを制御する手法「JCMC」を提案する。共有された行動測定空間内で予測された影響シグネチャを用い、目標効果と副作用の予算に基づいて介入を選択し、予測と観測を比較して保持またはロールバックを行う。滑らかさや有界推定などの仮定のもと、二次局所近似の境界や選択後悔の上限などを理論的に証明している。ベンチマーク測定は行わず、対照的推定量と評価プロトコルを定義し、既存の検索ベースラインとの比較枠組みを提示している。
