papers.title: What Matters for LLM Persona Simulation: Signal Form in Cold-Start E-Commerce Advertising
papers.summary: Estimating advertising performance in cold-start settings is challenging because historical logs are unavailable before launch. Large language models (LLMs) offer a potential alternative by simulating persona-conditioned user responses, but it remains unclear which design choices actually drive LLM-based persona simulation. Using real Google Ads e-commerce campaign data across five demographic segments, we identify three signal-form dimensions that affect simulation quality: (i) a demographic anchor without noisy rich attributes, (ii) a relative qualitative banner-blindness signal rather than quantitative anchors, and (iii) prompt phrasing. On this campaign, our method attains an MAE of 24.9 and a MAPE of 26.1%, a 51.3% lower MAE than the best tested non-LLM baseline and 77.3% lower than an LLM configuration using explicit CTR anchors. Systematic ablations show that minimal demographic descriptions achieve lower mean error than richer persona configurations, while relative qualitative cues substantially outperform the tested quantitative anchors. We additionally compare these configurations with direct-prior and rule-based baselines and with alternative LLM configurations.
papers.title_ja: LLMによるペルソナシミュレーションにおいて重要なのは何か：コールドスタートEC広告におけるシグナル形式
papers.summary_ja: コールドスタート環境における広告効果推定において、LLMを用いたペルソナシミュレーションの品質に影響を与える設計要素を特定した。人口統計情報のアンカー、相対的な定性的シグナル、プロンプトの表現の3点が重要であることを示し、豊富な属性情報よりも最小限の記述の方が誤差が低くなることを実証した。定量アンカーよりも相対的な定性的キューの方が優位であり、既存の非LLMベースラインや明示的なCTRアンカーを用いたLLM設定と比較して、MAEを大幅に低減する手法を提案した。
papers.relevance_reason: LLMの応用と評価手法が関心領域と一致

papers.title: Failure Profiling and Reachable Trajectory Selection for Reasoning Distillation
papers.summary: Training smaller language models on reasoning solutions generated by a larger teacher model is the prevailing approach for transferring mathematical reasoning capabilities. However, the student tends to overfit the output distribution of the teacher and generalizes poorly when its own behavior at inference time deviates from the training data. Recent methods attempt to bridge this gap by incorporating error data, yet the corrective trajectories still reflect the reasoning patterns of the teacher, which the student cannot reliably reproduce, leaving the distribution mismatch largely unresolved. We propose a method, Failure Profiling and Reachable Trajectory Selection (FPRT), built on the insight that effective training data should be jointly determined by what the student fails on and what it can realistically learn. Our method first profiles the failure behavior of the student on each problem through repeated sampling, characterizing it in terms of error rate and error consistency to reveal qualitatively distinct failure modes. Each mode demands a fundamentally different training signal. The diagnosed mode then guides candidate generation from the teacher via distinct prompting strategies tailored to each failure type. Among the correct candidates, our method selects the one whose initial reasoning steps after the point of divergence are most reproducible by the student. These first corrective steps constitute the primary bottleneck, while the remaining steps follow an already corrected context and can therefore be continued more readily. This contrasts with standard reranking approaches, which score the trajectory as a whole and thereby dilute the signal at the critical reasoning transition. Experiments demonstrate that our method achieves the SOTA performance across the five benchmarks on both student backbones.
papers.title_ja: 推論蒸留のための失敗プロファイリングと到達可能軌道選択
papers.summary_ja: 教師モデルの出力分布に過剰適合し、推論時の挙動が逸脱した際に汎化性能が低下する問題に対し、学生モデルの失敗特性を分析して学習データを最適化する手法FPRTを提案する。学生モデルの失敗モードを分類し、それに合わせたプロンプト戦略で教師モデルから候補解を生成する。さらに、分岐点直後の初期推論ステップが学生モデルによって再現可能かを基準に候補を絞り込むことで、重要な推論転換点での学習シグナルを強化する。5つのベンチマークにおいて、既存手法を上回るSOTA性能を達成した。
papers.relevance_reason: LLMの推論能力移転と効率化、ベンチマーク評価に直結する手法

papers.title: pESTO: Iterative p-greedy kernel regression with risk-driven Early STOpping
papers.summary: Kernel-based greedy algorithms select suitable approximation nodes by minimizing point-wise error indicators, such as the power function; in this context, they are usually referred to as p-greedy approaches. In the presence of noisy data, deterministic criteria may fail, as the discrepancy between the true solution and its estimate is influenced by both approximation error and noise amplification, and the balance between the two is unknown. This study explicitly separates these two contributions, which are governed by the power function and a Lebesgue-type term, respectively. These bounds motivate the use of the Stein's unbiased risk estimator (SURE) as a proxy of the mean squared error, which in turn provides a principled and computable stopping criterion for the number of nodes to select in the p-greedy procedure. Numerical experiments demonstrate that this approach effectively balances deterministic accuracy and statistical noise contributions.
papers.title_ja: pESTO: リスク駆動型早期停止を用いた反復p-greedyカーネル回帰
papers.summary_ja: ノイズを含むデータにおけるカーネルベースのp-greedyアルゴリズムの停止基準を改善する手法を提案する。近似誤差とノイズ増幅を分離し、Steinの無偏リスク推定量（SURE）を平均二乗誤差の代理指標として利用する。これにより、ノイズと精度のバランスを考慮した計算可能な停止条件を導出する。数値実験により、決定論的精度と統計的ノイズ寄与を効果的にバランスさせることが示された。
papers.relevance_reason: カーネル回帰とサロゲートモデル構築の最適化手法であり、ML手法全般に関心があるため高評価。

papers.title: Not All Misalignment Is Alike: A Decomposed Benchmark for Emergent Misalignment
papers.summary: Emergent misalignment (EM), in which fine-tuning on a narrow task induces misaligned behaviour on unrelated prompts, has been demonstrated across a wide range of datasets, model families, and training setups. Yet, most studies continue to rely on the evaluation approach introduced in the original EM paper, producing rates that are sensitive to the small set of evaluation questions used, the choice of judge, and the thresholds applied. These evaluations can also conflate misalignment with capability loss and offer little insight into the specific ways misalignment manifests. Differences in datasets, models, and fine-tuning configurations further make findings difficult to compare across studies. We introduce EMERGE, a decomposed benchmark that tracks changes in eight distinct misaligned behaviours from base to fine-tuned models. It evaluates these behaviours on out-of-domain prompts against matched benign controls and tracks capability, coherence, and refusal to account for potential confounders. Applying EMERGE to 8 open-weight models and 13 fine-tuning datasets, we find that models with similar broad misalignment rates can exhibit very different behavioural profiles that a single score cannot capture. We hope EMERGE can help establish a shared and robust standard for measuring EM, making findings more comparable and helping move research from detecting the phenomenon towards understanding it.
papers.title_ja: すべての不一致が同じではない：創発的ミズアライメントのための分解型ベンチマーク
papers.summary_ja: 本研究では、LLMのファインチューニングによって生じる「創発的ミズアライメント（EM）」を、従来の単一スコア評価ではなく、8つの異なる行動パターンに分解して評価するベンチマーク「EMERGE」を提案する。この手法は、能力低下や拒否応答などの混入要因を制御し、ベースモデルからファインチューニング後モデルまでの行動変化を詳細に追跡する。8つのオープンウェイトモデルと13つのデータセットへの適用により、全体の不一致率が類似していても、具体的な行動プロファイルが大きく異なることが明らかになった。これにより、EMの検出から理解へと研究を進展させ、比較可能な堅牢な評価基準を確立することを目的としている。
papers.relevance_reason: LLMの安全性評価・ベンチマーク設計に関心が高く、ハルシネーション対策とも関連

papers.title: An Educated Guess: Deriving Statistically Aligned Gradient Estimates for Zeroth-Order Optimisation
papers.summary: As novel hardware architectures are explored for the purposes of machine learning, including neuromorphic chips, asynchronous systems, and ASICs, effective learning algorithms are highly desirable. While backpropagation is the standard for differentiation on standard hardware, its requirement for global synchrony and exact differentiability limits the exploration of exotic algorithms on non-traditional substrates and devices. Zeroth-order (ZO) optimisation methods, such as SPSA and weight perturbation, offer a compelling alternative by estimating gradients through inference-only passes; however, these methods have historically suffered due to the `curse of dimensionality', where random perturbations become increasingly misaligned with the true gradient in high-dimensional spaces. In this work, we move beyond blind random noise by deriving zeroth-order search directions from activation geometry available during the forward pass. This leads to a family of Spectral Zeroth-Order methods, SZO-$\kappa$, whose directions solve local response-based gradient-guessing objectives under explicit stochastic assumptions. These methods explore feature-supported directions that are more likely to produce informative loss responses. Using multilayer and convolutional networks, we analyse gradient alignment, bias-variance structure, and training stability of these methods relative to standard perturbation baselines and backpropagation.
papers.title_ja: 賢明な推測：ゼロ次最適化のための統計的に整合した勾配推定導出
papers.summary_ja: ニューロモルフィックチップや非同期システムなど、バックプロパゲーションが困難なハードウェア向けに、推論パスのみで勾配を推定するゼロ次最適化手法の改善を提案する。従来のランダム摂動法が持つ次元の呪いを克服するため、フォワードパス中の活性化幾何学に基づき、局所的な応答を最大化する探索方向を導出する。これにより、Spectral Zeroth-Order (SZO) 手法族を定義し、多層パーセプトロンやCNNにおいて勾配整合性・バイアス分散構造・学習安定性を分析した。
papers.relevance_reason: ML手法全般と推論効率化に直結する革新的な最適化アルゴリズム

papers.title: Random Symbolic Boosting: A Geometric Approach to Symbolic Regression
papers.summary: Symbolic models offer interpretability, but their construction through generational evolution can be computationally expensive. This article presents Random Symbolic Boosting (RSB), a method that constructs explicit additive symbolic models via boosting over populations of randomly generated syntax trees, eliminating the need for generational evolution. The idea combines two observations: high-dimensional spaces can be spanned by enough linearly independent vectors, and the semantics of syntax trees can be directly manipulated as such vectors. It is shown that, for Ordinary Least Squares, the boosting process guarantees a monotonic reduction of the training error for both regression and classification. Furthermore, an adaptive geometric early stopping mechanism is introduced. It is based on the angle between the prediction and target vectors, is independent of the problems scale, and requires no adjustments across tasks. Evaluated on a standard benchmark for symbolic regression, the method is located at the Pareto-optimal point between predictive accuracy and training time, ranking first on the real-world datasets. Additionally, it was tested on a large tabular classification benchmark with 200 problems, achieving competitive results.
papers.title_ja: ランダムシンボリックブースティング：シンボリック回帰への幾何学的アプローチ
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、世代進化を不要とするシンボリック回帰手法「ランダムシンボリックブースティング（RSB）」を提案する。ランダムに生成した構文ツリーの集合に対してブースティングを適用し、明示的な加法型シンボリックモデルを構築することで、計算コストを大幅に削減する。最小二乗法において訓練誤差の単調減少を保証し、予測ベクトルと目標ベクトルの角度に基づくスケール非依存の適応型早期停止機構を導入する。標準ベンチマークでは予測精度と訓練時間のパレート最適点に位置し、実データセットで1位を獲得した。
papers.relevance_reason: 機械学習手法全般と評価ベンチマークへの関心に合致

papers.title: Lodos: A Lightweight Simulator Designed for Contact-Rich Interactions with Detailed Meshes
papers.summary: In recent years, massively parallelized rigid-body simulation has played a central role in robotics research, enabling rapid progress in areas such as reinforcement learning, stochastic optimal control, and randomized smoothing-based trajectory optimization. Particularly in contact-rich settings, the scalability of such simulations in large part depends on well-optimized representations of collision geometry, often requiring a coarse approximation of the underlying surfaces using primitives such as spheres, capsules, cylinders, and boxes. Whenever the complexity of the surfaces or the precision demands of the application render such approximations insufficient, it is instead necessary to employ mesh-mesh collisions, which impose a significant reduction in throughput. This paper proposes a simulation framework designed from scratch to address this bottleneck, with novel routines for broadphase and narrowphase collision detection as well as the subsequent contact dynamics computation. As experimentally validated, the framework matches existing well-established simulators in terms of physical faithfulness, and can achieve approximately an order of magnitude higher throughput in the detailed mesh-mesh collision setting that it specializes in. The source code is available at https://github.com/martius-lab/lodos.
papers.title_ja: Lodos: 詳細メッシュを用いた接触リッチな相互作用のための軽量シミュレータ
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、ロボティクス研究における剛体シミュレーションのボトルネックである、詳細メッシュ同士の衝突検出と接触力学計算を高速化する軽量シミュレータ「Lodos」を提案する。既存のシミュレータが球や箱などのプリミティブによる粗い近似に依存するのに対し、Lodosはブロードフェーズおよびナローフェーズの衝突検出アルゴリズムを新規に設計し、物理的忠実度を維持しつつスループットを約1桁向上させる。強化学習や確率的最適制御など、高精度な接触シミュレーションが求められる分野での計算効率化に貢献する。
papers.relevance_reason: 強化学習の基盤となるシミュレーション効率化だが、軌道力学やLLMとは直接無関係

papers.title: The multiplier step size in classical two-block ADMM: convergence and counterexamples
papers.summary: How large can the multiplier step be in the classical two-block alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM)? We keep the penalty fixed and use the usual primal updates. We consider finite-dimensional problems with closed proper convex objectives. We assume that a Karush-Kuhn-Tucker point exists and that each block subproblem attains its minimum at every step. Under these assumptions, the constraint images and the multiplier converge for a range of factors that extends beyond the golden ratio. The constraint matrices may be rank deficient. For larger steps, we construct two fixed compact polytopes and give an explicit threshold below two. The polytopes admit an infeasible periodic orbit for every factor at or above this threshold. At that threshold, ADMM can cycle even for smooth strongly convex objectives. This gives a negative answer to Glowinski's question about the full interval from zero to two. A different pair of piecewise-quadratic objectives gives geometrically growing residuals. For the general convex class, we locate the endpoint of the uniform convergence interval near 1.88688256. A convergence certificate on the unit circle gives the lower bound, while a separate periodic orbit gives the upper bound. Exact arithmetic verifies that the two bounds differ by less than 0.000000174.
papers.title_ja: 古典的2ブロックADMMにおける乗数ステップサイズ：収束性と反例
papers.summary_ja: 古典的な2ブロックADMMアルゴリズムにおいて、ペナルティ係数を固定した際の乗数ステップサイズの収束限界を解析した。黄金比を超えた範囲での収束性を示す一方で、特定の多面体構造を用いて、ステップサイズが一定の閾値を超えると滑らかな強凸目的関数であっても周期軌道（サイクル）が発生することを証明した。これにより、Glowinskiが提唱した0から2までの全区間での収束性に関する問いに対して否定的な回答を与えた。さらに、一般の凸クラスにおける一様収束区間の端点を約1.88688256と高精度で特定し、理論的な境界を厳密に決定した。
papers.relevance_reason: 凸最適化アルゴリズムの理論的限界に関する研究であり、ML手法全般に関係するが、LLMや軌道力学とは直接無関係。

papers.title: Higher Order Component Attribution via Learned Surrogates in High Energy Physics
papers.summary: Experimental High Energy Physics (HEP) has adopted the transformer architecture for identification of jets, particularly the state-of-the-art Particle Transformer (ParT) which injects explicit information about particle correlations into the attention mechanism. While able to achieve state-of-the-art results in accuracy, interpretability to its effectiveness has been limited. In this paper we propose component attribution methods using Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) that directly tie back to the physical descriptors of jets, to probe whether mechanisms such as Multi-Head Attention (MHA), or the ParT architecture, are able to learn these as discriminating features.
papers.title_ja: 高エネルギー物理学における学習済みサロゲートを用いた高次コンポーネント帰属
papers.summary_ja: 高エネルギー物理学におけるジェット識別に用いられるParticle Transformer（ParT）の解釈可能性を高める手法を提案する。Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks（KAN）を用いたコンポーネント帰属分析により、モデル内部のメカニズムが物理記述子とどのように結びついているかを定量的に評価する。Multi-Head AttentionやParT特有の構造が、識別特徴として物理的に意味のある情報を学習しているかを検証する。これにより、ブラックボックス化しがちな深層学習モデルの内部動作を物理的観点から解明する枠組みを提供する。
papers.relevance_reason: サロゲートモデルと解釈可能性の手法は関連するが、対象分野がHEPであり軌道力学とは異なるため。

papers.title: Topology as a Design Variable: Joint Architecture-Sizing Optimization for SRAM
papers.summary: SRAM's power-performance-area-stability trade-off depends on bitcell topology, a discrete architectural choice that interacts non-separably with continuous transistor sizing. However, no open-source SRAM tool treats topology as an optimizable variable. OpenRAM generates SRAM layouts but performs no optimization, while OpenYield supports high-fidelity evaluation but restricts optimization to scalar sizing of a fixed 6T cell. OpenYieldV2 closes this gap through three integrated contributions. First, a fully parameterized compiler generates complete 6T and 10T SRAM macros with peripheral circuits and replica-bitline self-timing, enabling topology comparison under identical simulation conditions. Second, a few-shot TabPFN surrogate learns topology-dependent PPA responses with limited full-macro SPICE samples. Third, a coarse-to-refined multi-objective optimizer combines global exploration of discrete architectural choices with local refinement of continuous transistor sizes. Experiments across varying design conditions reveal a topology decision boundary that shifts with operating constraints rather than following a fixed design rule. Jointly optimizing across this boundary improves hypervolume by up to 17.3\% over the strongest single-topology baseline. OpenYieldV2 is open-source to support reproducible SRAM design research.
papers.title_ja: トポロジーを設計変数として：SRAMにおけるアーキテクチャとサイズングの同時最適化
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、SRAMの設計において離散的なビットセルトポロジーと連続的なトランジスタサイズを同時に最適化するオープンソースツール「OpenYieldV2」を提案する。TabPFNを用いた少サンプルサロゲートモデルでPPA特性を予測し、粗から細への多目的最適化アルゴリズムにより、離散アーキテクチャ選択と連続サイズ調整を統合的に探索する。実験により、動作制約に応じて変化するトポロジーの境界が示され、単一トポロジーベースライン比でハイパボリューメが最大17.3%向上することが確認された。
papers.relevance_reason: サロゲートモデルと最適化手法は関心領域だが、対象が半導体設計であり軌道力学とは無関係

papers.title: Zero-Query Transferable Pretend Benign Attacks with Amortized Online Generation for Cooperative Perception
papers.summary: Cooperative perception enables an ego agent to acquire information from collaborators beyond its own sensors' reach. Yet, the most beneficial messages are often the hardest to verify from local observations. Pretend Benign (PB) exploits this asymmetry by targeting regions with weak local verifiability and applying multi-objective perturbations, making harmful feature changes appear to be benign assistance. However, PB is victim-dependent: selecting regions and optimizing perturbations require the victim model's architecture, parameters, and gradients, limiting transfer to unseen victims. A transferable attack must capture properties shared across cooperative detection models rather than those specific to one network. We address this by building a victim-agnostic attack from a heterogeneous ensemble of surrogate models and encoding its capabilities in a reusable dictionary to reduce per-message generation cost. Specifically, Transferable Pretend Benign (TrPB) transfers PB's region selection criterion and multi-objective perturbation strategy across heterogeneous surrogates to construct an offline attack. We further propose RT-TrPB, which encodes transferable regions and perturbation patterns into a region predictor and reusable perturbation dictionary, amortizing per-message attack generation. Experiments on widely used cooperative perception benchmarks show that RT-TrPB bypasses the consensus-based defenses ROBOSAC and FLD with success rates approaching 100% and generates each perturbation in under 56 ms. To counter PB-style attacks masquerading as benign collaboration, we also propose STTrust, which verifies received messages using spatial and temporal consistency and incorporates identity-level trust. STTrust detects over 90% of PB-style attacks and restores perception performance to near the attack-free level.
papers.title_ja: 協調知覚における償却オンライン生成を用いたゼロクエリ転移可能な偽装無害攻撃
papers.summary_ja: 協調知覚システムにおける敵対的攻撃手法「Pretend Benign (PB)」の転移可能性を高めることを目的とした研究である。異種サロゲートモデルのアンサンブルを用いて被害者非依存の攻撃を構築し、領域予測器と再利用可能な摂動辞書によりメッセージ生成コストを償却するRT-TrPBを提案した。実験では、既存の防御機構をほぼ100%の成功率で回避し、1メッセージあたり56ms未満で攻撃を生成できることを示した。また、空間・時間的一貫性とアイデンティティ信頼度を用いた防御手法STTrustも提案し、90%以上の攻撃検出率と性能回復を実現した。
papers.relevance_reason: サロゲートモデル活用と効率化手法は関心と一致するが、対象が協調知覚のセキュリティであり軌道力学やLLM推論とは直接無関係。

papers.title: Does Country Matter? Evaluating Geographic Sensitivity of Large Language Models in Zero-Shot Chronic Kidney Disease Screening
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) show strong zero-shot reasoning capabilities, yet their sensitivity to prompt context raises questions about reliability in deployment. This study investigates whether geographic context embedded in prompts influences LLM-based chronic kidney disease (CKD) screening, independent of any change in patient features. Using a community-based CKD dataset from Bangladesh (284 participants with 112 CKD and 172 non-CKD), we systematically varied the country attribute across 25 global contexts while holding all clinical inputs constant, and evaluated two open-weight LLMs (Qwen3 8B and Mistral 7B). Experiments were conducted on a common-correct subset of 156 participants for whom both models produced correct baseline predictions. Results show that non-CKD predictions were highly stable across geographic contexts, with both models maintaining consistent non-CKD predictions in nearly all settings. In contrast, CKD-positive predictions were considerably more sensitive. For Qwen3, CKD prediction dropped from a baseline of 65 to as low as 50 across country contexts, while Mistral showed smaller but non-negligible variation. Country contexts did not group according to known epidemiological or healthcare similarities; instead, groupings appear to reflect how country tokens are internally represented within each model. These findings demonstrate that geographic tokens can systematically shift clinical screening outcomes despite identical patient inputs, with implications for the deployment of LLM-based decision support in diverse healthcare settings.
papers.title_ja: 国は重要か？ゼロショット慢性腎臓病スクリーニングにおける大規模言語モデルの地理的感度の評価
papers.summary_ja: 本研究は、プロンプト内の地理的コンテキスト（国名）が、患者の臨床データを変えずにLLMによる慢性腎臓病（CKD）スクリーニング結果に与える影響を調査した。バングラデシュのデータセットを用い、Qwen3 8BとMistral 7Bの2つのオープンウェイトLLMで25カ国のコンテキストをテストした結果、CKD陽性予測は国名によって大きく変動することが判明した。特にQwen3では陽性予測数が65から50まで低下し、モデル内部の国トークン表現が予測結果を系統的にシフトさせることが示された。この発見は、多様な医療環境でのLLMベースの意思決定支援システムの信頼性評価において、地理的バイアスの考慮が不可欠であることを示唆している。
papers.relevance_reason: LLMの信頼性評価に関わるが、医療特化であり軌道力学や効率化とは無関係

papers.title: RL-ATTACK: A Generalized Black-Box Adversarial Attack on Language Models via Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) exhibit vulnerabilities to adversarial perturbations that can induce unintended responses. These vulnerabilities can be identified via intentional attacks and subsequently used to improve model safety. In black-box settings where gradients are inaccessible, existing methods tend to guess adversarial transformations using external knowledge, ignoring the information provided by the target model. To mitigate this, we propose a trainable black-box framework based on reinforcement learning, which learns from the target model to generate tailored adversarial transformations. We demonstrate that our approach achieves lower post-attack accuracy, greater query efficiency and better semantic preservation on both natural language inference and generative Q&A tasks. On natural language inference, it drives post-attack accuracy to 2% within 20 queries. Against generative language models, our trained attacker consistently achieves lower post-attack accuracy than the untrained attacker and wins in 4 out of 6 settings when compared to a strong optimization-based baseline. We further experiment with multiple reward designs and training settings, and we find that no design or setting is consistently dominant. Our code is available at https://github.com/taikunudel/RL-ATTACK.
papers.title_ja: RL-ATTACK: 強化学習による言語モデルへの汎用的ブラックボックス敵対的攻撃
papers.summary_ja: 勾配情報が得られないブラックボックス環境において、強化学習を用いてターゲットモデルの反応から敵対的変換を学習するフレームワークを提案する。既存手法が外部知識に依存するのに対し、本手法はモデル自身のフィードバックを活用し、クエリ効率と意味保存性を向上させる。自然言語推論タスクでは20クエリ以内で攻撃後の精度を2%まで低下させ、生成型Q&Aタスクでも強力な最適化ベースのベースラインを上回る性能を示した。報酬設計や学習設定の影響についても検証し、一貫して優位な設定が存在しないことを確認している。
papers.relevance_reason: 強化学習とLLMの組み合わせだが、攻撃特化で効率化や軌道力学とは無関係

papers.title: On the Few-Shot Adaptation of Vision-Language Models: A Few Gradient Signs Are All You Need
papers.summary: The limited supervision available for the few-shot adaptation of vision-language models makes gradient estimation particularly noisy. We find that the gradient magnitudes are severely miscalibrated, while the signs of a small top-magnitude subset remain informative. This motivates SignSparseSGD and DynSignSparseSGD, two state-free optimizers that use gradient magnitudes only to select where to update and fixed-magnitude signs to decide how to update. The static variant fixes the support after the first minibatch. The dynamic variant refreshes it at every step. Across 11 datasets, three CLIP backbones, and five shot levels, the proposed methods are competitive with or outperform parameter-efficient and optimization-based baselines on average, while exhibiting markedly lower sensitivity to long training schedules. They introduce no task-specific modules, maintain no first- or second-moment optimizer states, and use one shared configuration across datasets, backbones, and shot levels. Our code is included in the supplementary materials and will be released upon publication.
papers.title_ja: 視覚言語モデルの少ショット適応について：少数の勾配符号だけで十分である
papers.summary_ja: 視覚言語モデルの少ショット適応において、勾配の大きさが大きく誤って推定される一方、上位の少数の勾配符号は情報量を持つことを発見した。これに基づき、勾配の大きさで更新箇所を選択し、固定の符号で更新方向を決定する状態不要型オプティマイザ「SignSparseSGD」と「DynSignSparseSGD」を提案する。11データセット・3種のCLIPバックボーン・5段階のショットレベルで検証し、パラメータ効率型ベースラインと同等以上の性能を示しつつ、長期学習スケジュールへの感度が低いことを確認した。タスク固有モジュールやオプティマイザ状態を必要とせず、全設定で共通の構成を使用可能である。

papers.title: Reconstructing LLM Lineage Trees via Fine-Tuning Path Inference
papers.summary: Fine-tuned (FT) derivatives of large language models (LLMs) are now released in large numbers, yet their provenance relies on self-reports and cannot be verified. Misattributed lineage leaves a verifier unable to audit outsourced fine-tuning, confirm license compliance of derived models, or trace vulnerabilities that a parent passes to its children. All three require the direction of derivation, not merely its presence. Existing output-only methods are limited to pairwise derivation tests or undirected lineage estimation, while recovering a directed tree requires white-box access to model weights. We formalize the problem of reconstructing a directed model tree, including internal nodes, under gray-box access, where only teacher-forced log-likelihoods are observed and weights are never inspected. Fine-tuning raises the log-likelihood of the training data, and a child inherits this increase from its parent. Building on this property, we define an asymmetric per-task log-likelihood deviation between any two models as a trace of fine-tuning history, and derive from it an edge weight for each ordered pair of models. We propose TRACE-Edge, which exactly solves for the maximum spanning directed tree under these edge weights, with neither hyperparameters nor tree-structure constraints. We evaluate it on five configurations totaling 25 model trees built from three base models and seven tasks. TRACE-Edge achieves a parent-match accuracy of 0.74 when probed with the fine-tuning examples, and on average outperforms an output-similarity baseline even with held-out probes drawn from the same distribution as the training data.
papers.title_ja: ファインチューニング経路の推論によるLLM系譜ツリーの再構築
papers.summary_ja: 大規模言語モデル（LLM）のファインチューニング派生モデルの系譜（どのモデルが親か）を、重みへのアクセスなしに推定する手法を提案する。教師強制ログ尤度を用いた非対称な偏差をエッジ重みとし、最大生成有向木を厳密に解くTRACE-Edgeアルゴリズムを設計した。5つの設定・25本のモデルツリーで評価し、ファインチューニング例を用いた場合の親マッチ精度は0.74に達した。出力類似性ベースラインを上回る性能を示し、ライセンス遵守や脆弱性追跡への応用が期待される。
papers.relevance_reason: LLM関連だが、効率化や推論高速化という関心とは異なる系譜推定が主眼

papers.title: KnowEvo: Knowledge Evolution for Protein Optimization
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) have shown promise in scientific discovery, yet systematically accumulating and refining reusable scientific knowledge remains challenging. Existing approaches primarily improve LLM-based problem solving through parameter optimization or feedback-driven refinement of prompts, programs, and solution trajectories, leaving acquired expertise either embedded in model weights or scattered across iterative problem-solving processes. As a result,knowledge is difficult to systematically inspect, evaluate, and refine. We propose KnowEvo, a framework that treats externalized knowledge itself as the optimization target. Our key insight is that scientific knowledge is inherently modular: multiple interacting mechanisms jointly determine the design outcomes. This makes knowledge evolution fundamentally challenging, as improvements cannot be attributed to individual components in isolation. To address this, KnowEvo represents knowledge as executable expertise blocks and organizes their refinements into strategy mutation trees, enabling structured exploration over a combinatorial knowledge space. The framework combines a Thompson-style forward allocation strategy that adaptively distributes evaluation budgets across strategy variants with a backward revision process, in which a code agent operates in an isolated sandbox to translate rollout evidence into localized program updates. This design enables persistent accumulation, evaluation, and refinement of mechanistic expertise across iterative experimentation. We evaluate KnowEvo on protein optimization tasks including stability and solubility. Results show that knowledge evolution consistently improves over initial strategy blocks and outperforms monolithic program evolution and prior LLM-guided evolution baselines across metrics such as pass@k, MRR, MAP,and NDCG@5. Code is available at https://github.com/recynie/KnowEvo.
papers.title_ja: KnowEvo: タンパク質最適化のための知識進化
papers.summary_ja: LLMを用いた科学発見において、再利用可能な知識の蓄積と洗練が課題である現状に対し、外部化された知識そのものを最適化対象とするフレームワークKnowEvoを提案する。科学知識は複数の相互作用するメカニズムから成るモジュール性を持つため、知識を実行可能なエキスパートブロックとして表現し、戦略変異ツリーを用いて構造化された探索を行う。Thompsonサンプリングに基づく予算配分戦略と、サンドボックス内でコードエージェントがローカルなプログラム更新を行う後方修正プロセスを組み合わせることで、反復実験を通じて持続的に知識を蓄積・評価・洗練する。タンパク質の安定性や溶解性などの最適化タスクにおいて、従来のLLM主導進化ベースラインや単一プログラム進化を上回る性能を示した。

papers.title: When Can You Trust Neural Critics? Auditing Mutual Information Estimates of Higher-Order Epistasis in Protein Language Models
papers.summary: Mutual information (MI) estimation is used to probe what neural representations encode, including in protein language models, but variational MI estimators have variance that scales at least exponentially in the true MI. We audit a prior neural-MI study of order-resolved epistasis in ESM-2 on the four-site GB1 landscape. Run-to-run differences show no systematic bias and a magnitude comparable to ordinary cross-seed retraining variability, and the evaluation-pairing scheme shifts scores substantially. At the original dimensionality, two of three alternative estimator families stabilize the estimate across seeds and one does not. In a synthetic calibration at the representation dimensionalities of two other protein language models (a Gaussian channel with known MI; no model representations), all three families recover materially less signal than required, despite correct signal ordering and stable seeds. A control critic given the true signal direction, which also reduces its input to one dimension, recovers 93.3% and 98.7% of the analytic MI at gain 1.5 (at 5,120 and 4,096 dimensions), so the signal is recoverable with privileged information, but the control does not identify why blind estimation fails. We package the checks into a reusable diagnostic protocol and conclude that even a stabilized estimator is not currently sufficient for order-resolved dependence claims made under blind search at this dimensionality and sample size.
papers.title_ja: ニューラルクリティッカーを信頼できるのはいつか？タンパク質言語モデルにおける高次エピスタシスの相互情報量推定監査
papers.summary_ja: タンパク質言語モデル（PLM）の表現が持つ高次エピスタシス（相互作用）を相互情報量（MI）で評価する際、変分推定器の分散が指数関数的に増大する問題を検証した。ESM-2を用いた先行研究の再現性監査と、既知のMIを持つ合成データによるキャリブレーションを通じて、既存の推定器が盲検検索下では真の信号を十分に回復できないことを示した。特権情報を与えた制御実験では信号の回復が可能である一方、盲検推定では失敗する要因を特定し、現在の手法では高次依存関係の主張を支持するには不十分であると結論づけた。
papers.relevance_reason: LLM評価手法だが、対象がタンパク質特化で軌道力学と無関係

papers.title: FasterRW: An Efficient Prior-Assisted Random Walk Solver for Thermal Analysis
papers.summary: Thermal simulation is becoming increasingly critical in modern IC design and manufacturing. Feynman--Kac random walk methods can estimate localized temperatures without solving the global field, but in practical settings without Dirichlet boundaries they require very long paths to control the truncation residual. This paper presents FasterRW, a continuation-value framework for accelerating Feynman--Kac thermal random walks. We prove a stopping-time residual identity showing that the expected tail after truncation equals the current attenuation weight multiplied by the temperature at the stopping location. This identity enables a prior-corrected single-point estimator: a cheap, noisy prior replaces the unknown continuation value, making the truncation bias scale with prior error rather than absolute temperature and yielding an error-controlled threshold-selection rule. For multi-point queries, FasterRW further converts cross-query pass-through tails into pseudo-samples and refines the resulting observations in prior-error coordinates through kriging. Compared with prior state-of-the-art methods, FasterRW achieves up to $28\times$ acceleration while maintaining accuracy. Our code is open-sourced at https://github.com/ShiningSord/FastRW.
papers.title_ja: FasterRW: 熱解析のための効率的な事前情報支援ランダムウォークソルバ
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、IC設計における熱シミュレーションの高速化を目的としたFasterRW手法を提案する。Feynman-Kacランダムウォーク法における打ち切り残差を事前情報で補正し、バイアスを事前誤差に依存させることで精度を維持しつつ計算コストを削減する。さらに、多点クエリに対してクリギングを用いて観測値を洗練させることで、既存手法比最大28倍の高速化を実現した。
papers.relevance_reason: サロゲートモデルや推論高速化の手法として関連するが、対象が熱解析であり軌道力学ではないため中程度。

papers.title: Generative Reconstruction of Full-Field Sensor States for Safety-Critical Digital Twins
papers.summary: Accurate reconstruction of incomplete sensor fields is critical for state awareness in safety-critical digital twins (DTs). Thermocouples in high-temperature and radiation environments may drift, fail, or become intermittently unavailable, causing partial observability. This study develops a sparse-sensor reconstruction framework for Oregon State University's High Temperature Test Facility (HTTF) and evaluates six methods under intra- and inter-experiment protocols: three conditional generative models (i.e., a diffusion model [DM], variational autoencoder [VAE], and generative adversarial network [GAN]), two deterministic recurrent neural-network models, and ridge regression. For intra-experiment reconstruction within the PG{-}29 depressurized conduction cooldown (DCC) test, the models combine graph-based spatial encoding with gated recurrent units. The graph neural network (GNN)--gated recurrent unit (GRU) VAE achieves the lowest error, with a mean absolute error (MAE) of $11.73,^\circ$C, a root mean square error (RMSE) of $20.54,^\circ$C, and an $R^2$ of 0.98. The deterministic GNN--GRU and plain GRU obtain RMSE values of $25.26,^\circ$C and $35.22,^\circ$C, respectively, demonstrating the benefit of spatial modeling. All three generative models reduce RMSE by more than half compared with ridge regression. The DM maintains an $R^2$ of 0.94 when known sensors decrease from 91 to 45. For inter-experiment reconstruction, models trained on PG{-}27 pressurized conduction cooldown (PCC) are evaluated on PG{-}29 using section-context conditioning. The section-context DM achieves the best transfer performance, with an RMSE of $42.84,^\circ$C and an $R^2$ of 0.91. These results demonstrate the value of spatiotemporal generative modeling for missing-sensor reconstruction in safety-critical DT applications.
papers.title_ja: 安全性が重要なデジタルツインにおける全フィールドセンサー状態の生成再構築
papers.summary_ja: 高温・放射線環境下でセンサーが欠損した場合のデジタルツイン向けに、スパースセンサーからの状態再構築フレームワークを提案した。拡散モデル、VAE、GANなどの生成モデルと、GNN-GRUを組み合わせた決定論的モデルを比較評価した。実験内再構築ではGNN-GRU VAEが最も低い誤差を示し、空間モデリングの優位性を証明した。また、実験間転移学習においてもセクションコンテキスト付き拡散モデルが優れた汎化性能を発揮した。
papers.relevance_reason: 深層学習手法の適用だが、対象が宇宙軌道やLLM効率化ではないため中程度

papers.title: Adaptive Depth Aggregation in Graph Transformers for Long-Range Graph Reasoning
papers.summary: Graph Transformers improve long-range node-to-node communication through global or structure-aware interactions. However, improving cross-node communication does not determine how computations produced at different depths should be combined. Standard residual streams accumulate successive computations with fixed unit coefficients shared across nodes. This fixed aggregation is a residual-interface constraint: once intermediate contributions have been produced, the interface cannot explicitly reweight them by node. We hypothesize that this constraint can create a depth-wise aggregation mismatch when the relative utility of these intermediate contributions varies across nodes and structural contexts. To study this hypothesis, we formalize Graph Transformer residual computation as a causal node-wise history of graph-propagation and feed-forward network (FFN) contributions, making depth aggregation an explicit interface choice. We realize node-adaptive aggregation over this history with Attention Residuals (AttnRes) while preserving the backbone's graph-propagation and auxiliary-state machinery. Block AttnRes reduces the routing cost of long histories relative to Full AttnRes by pooling consecutive contributions. We instantiate the interface in GPS and GRIT and evaluate it on all five ECHO tasks. Both variants achieve lower mean absolute error (MAE) than their independently tuned backbones on every task, and at least one obtains the lowest mean among all compared methods in each task. Routing-only donor-swap interventions support the mismatch hypothesis, while additional ablations examine the key design choices. Together, these results support node-adaptive depth aggregation as a useful complement to cross-node communication in long-range graph reasoning.
papers.title_ja: 長距離グラフ推論のためのグラフトランスフォーマーにおける適応的深さ集約
papers.summary_ja: グラフトランスフォーマーにおける標準的な残差接続の固定係数による制約を指摘し、ノードごとに中間計算の重みを適応的に調整する「Attention Residuals (AttnRes)」を提案する。この手法は、グラフ伝播とFFNの寄与を因果的な履歴として形式化し、ブロック単位でのプーリングによりルーティングコストを削減する。GPSおよびGRITモデルに適用し、ECHOタスク5種すべてで既存手法を上回る精度（MAE低減）を達成した。ノード適応的な深さ集約が、長距離グラフ推論におけるノード間通信の重要な補完要素であることを示した。
papers.relevance_reason: 深層学習のアーキテクチャ改善だが、軌道力学やLLM効率化との直接関連は薄い

papers.title: ELPAC: Endpoint-Anchored Latent Progression with Stage-Varying Multimodal Coordination
papers.summary: Aging cohorts increasingly combine imaging, plasma, and cognitive measurements, but most subjects provide only a partially observed cross-sectional snapshot, leaving latent stage, progression subtype, and stage-varying multimodal coordination to be inferred jointly. Existing methods estimate the cohort-level aging process, model covariance under observed covariates, or fuse modalities for prediction. However, they rarely target the joint problem of endpoint-anchored staging and progression-resolved residual coordination across modalities, even though subject staging, subtype assignment, and multimodal interplay are mutually dependent. We introduce ELPAC, a Bayesian framework with two interlocking constructions. The first integrates subtype trajectories backward from clinically reliable endpoint groups along biologically structured velocity components encoding modality-specific monotone direction and optional sequential ordering priors. The second factorizes residual multimodal variation around the inferred stage axis into sparse coordination axes whose loadings and activations expose which multimodal patterns are operative in each subtype and when they emerge, with stage-resolved variation supplying the auxiliary structure for conditional identifiability. We use a scalable amortized variational inference scheme that enables joint posterior inference at cohort scale with single-pass deployment on new subjects. On synthetic data and a harmonized ADNI+NACC/SCAN Alzheimer's cohort, ELPAC demonstrates accurate latent-structure recovery, well-calibrated prediction intervals, and biologically interpretable multimodal coordination programs that differ by subtype.
papers.title_ja: ELPAC: エンドポイントアンカー型潜在進行とステージ変動マルチモーダル協調
papers.summary_ja: アルツハイマー病などの加齢コホートにおいて、部分観測データから潜在ステージ・進行サブタイプ・マルチモーダル協調を同時に推定するベイズフレームワーク「ELPAC」を提案する。臨床的に信頼できるエンドポイント群から後方積分するサブタイプ軌道と、ステージ軸周りの残差変動をスパースな協調軸に分解する2つの構成要素からなる。スケーラブルな償却変分推論によりコホート規模での同時後方推定と新規被験者への単一パス適用を実現する。合成データとADNI+NACC/SCANコホートにおいて、潜在構造の正確な復元、較正された予測区間、およびサブタイプごとに異なる生物学的に解釈可能なマルチモーダル協調プログラムの抽出を示した。

papers.title: Evolutionary Adaptive Metric Learning: A Multi-Objective Framework for Learning Local Distance Functions in Nearest Neighbor Classification
papers.summary: Nearest neighbour classifiers inherit the geometry of their distance function. Fixed distances and globally learned metrics apply the same geometry throughout the input space, although relevant feature directions may vary across regions. We propose EAML (Evolutionary Adaptive Metric Learning), a framework that learns instance-dependent positive-definite metrics through a low-dimensional parameterization. Each local metric combines an input-dependent diagonal scaling, generated by softmax interpolation between anchor points, with a global low-rank correlation component. A real-coded elitist genetic algorithm optimizes the parameters using a scalar objective combining leave-one-out prediction error, robustness, metric smoothness, and regularization. We establish positive definiteness, metric equivalence, existence of an optimal solution, and Lipschitz continuity of the metric field. We further investigate prediction stability, generalization bounds, and evolutionary convergence under explicit assumptions. Experiments on synthetic data with region-dependent feature relevance show that EAML can recover local metric variations and outperform global metrics. Evaluation on thirteen public datasets using nested 5-fold cross-validation reveals a more nuanced picture: EAML improves performance on selected datasets but does not significantly outperform global metric baselines overall. Additional experiments show that global diagonal metrics can be preferable under nuisance features and test-time noise. These findings identify the conditions under which evolutionary local metric learning is beneficial and highlight its practical limitations.
papers.title_ja: 進化的適応メトリック学習：近傍分類における局所距離関数の学習のための多目的フレームワーク
papers.summary_ja: 入力空間の領域ごとに最適な距離計量（メトリック）が異なる問題に対し、アンカー点間のsoftmax補間と低ランク成分を用いた低次元パラメータ化により、インスタンス依存の正定値メトリックを学習するフレームワークEAMLを提案する。実数コードのエリート遺伝的アルゴリズムを用いて、予測誤差・頑健性・滑らかさ・正則化を統合したスカラー目的関数を最適化し、メトリック場の正定値性やLipschitz連続性などの理論的性質を確立した。合成データでは局所メトリックの変化を回復しグローバルメトリックを上回るが、13個の公開データセットでの評価では全体的な優位性は示せず、ノイズや不要特徴量がある条件下ではグローバル対角メトリックが優れる場合があることを明らかにした。

papers.title: Q-OIL: Optimistic Exploration in Learning from Human Interventions
papers.summary: As robots are deployed in the real world, they will inevitably make mistakes. Human interventions provide valuable feedback for improving their behavior, enabling them to adapt online to new scenarios. However, studying human-in-the-loop robot learning is difficult: real-world experiments are slow and expensive, so most algorithm development relies on simulated human models. We show that common human modeling assumptions do not match how real people intervene in practice. Through analyzing intervention data from human participants, we find that humans tend to intervene when agent progress stalls, and that their corrective actions are often suboptimal. Motivated by these findings, we introduce a progress-based model of human intervention that achieves higher rank correlation with real-user algorithm rankings, enabling realistic algorithm benchmarking and development in simulation. Building on these insights, we propose Q-OIL, a method that adds optimistic bonuses to intervention transitions in reinforcement learning and softly guides exploration toward human corrections. We find that decoupled critics are critical for stability because they prevent the bonuses from backing up to pre-intervention states. As a result, Q-OIL learns more efficiently than competitive baselines, achieving 10-50% higher success in simulation and on real robots, and improving pretrained VLAs on two bimanual manipulation tasks. As we ground both evaluation and algorithms in realistic human behavior, this work provides a practical path toward scalable robot learning from interventions.
papers.title_ja: Q-OIL: 人間の介入からの学習における楽観的探索
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、ロボットの人間介入データ分析に基づき、人間の介入行動をより現実的にモデル化する手法を提案する。従来の仮定と異なる人間の行動特性（進捗停滞時の介入、非最適な修正動作）を反映した評価環境を構築し、アルゴリズム開発の信頼性を向上させた。さらに、強化学習において介入遷移に楽観的ボーナスを加えるQ-OIL手法を提案し、探索を人間の修正方向へソフトに誘導する。この手法により、シミュレーションおよび実ロボットでの成功率が10〜50%向上し、事前学習済みVLAモデルの性能改善も示された。
papers.relevance_reason: 強化学習とエージェント設計に関わるが、宇宙・軌道力学とは無関係

papers.title: Meituan-Robotics-0: A Vision-Language-Action Foundation Model for Desktop Manipulation
papers.summary: We present Meituan-Robotics-0 (MR0), a vision-language-action foundation model and embodied-agent system for stationary-base desktop manipulation. MR0 combines 147 million vision-language samples with 15,060 hours of curated robot trajectories spanning 12 embodiments. A three-stage training recipe aligns multimodal representations with robot behavior through discrete action-token pre-training, transfers these priors to continuous cross-embodiment control through flow-matching mid-training, and adapts the policy through real-world post-training. We introduce Rollback, which pairs replaced policy segments with human corrections to provide positive and negative supervision for CFG-DAgger without value learning or advantage labeling. A unified end-effector interface supports heterogeneous embodiments, while asynchronous action-chunk merging maintains smooth execution under variable inference latency. An event-driven agent maintains persistent task events and reassesses plans when progress or feasibility changes, enabling cross-task retrieval and conditional task resumption. MR0 achieves 93.6% success on RoboTwin 2.0 and ranks fifth in the RoboDojo VLA track. Under matched HG-DAgger post-training, MR0 achieves higher average success rate and progress score than $\pi_{0.5}$ across three real-robot tasks. On Ethernet insertion, CFG-DAgger trained with Rollback data reaches 70% success and a progress score of 0.90. Qualitative agent deployments demonstrate cross-task event retrieval and recovery from temporarily unsatisfied task conditions.
papers.title_ja: Meituan-Robotics-0: デスクトップ操作のためのビジョン・言語・アクション基盤モデル
papers.summary_ja: 固定ベースのデスクトップ操作を対象とした、ビジョン・言語・アクション（VLA）基盤モデル「Meituan-Robotics-0」を提案する。1億4,700万の視覚言語サンプルと15,060時間のロボット軌道データを用い、離散アクショントークンの事前学習、フローマッチングによる連続制御への転移、実環境での後学習という3段階の訓練レシピを採用した。人間による修正を正負の教師信号として活用する「Rollback」手法や、推論遅延を吸収する非同期アクションチャンクマージング、イベント駆動型のエージェント設計により、RoboTwin 2.0で93.6%の成功率を達成し、既存モデルと比較して高い汎用性と安定性を示した。

papers.title: ForPC: Force-Aware Whole-Body Control for Precise Humanoid Cart Pushing
papers.summary: Humanoid robots are expected to take over strenuous material handling in manufacturing, logistics, and healthcare, where operating existing wheeled carts would let them move heavy loads without modifying the workplace. However, humanoid cart pushing remains challenging because the bimanual grasp closes a force-coupled loop in which the contact wrenches that drive the cart also disturb the robot's balance, and payload changes alter the coupled dynamics. We propose ForPC, a force-aware whole-body control framework that regulates cart velocity through two-stage reinforcement learning. A locomotion prior is first trained under varied hand loads and upper-body postures to provide balance support. A force latent and a state latent are then inferred from onboard observations, without external force sensors, and fed to a residual policy that coordinates bounded arm, waist, and leg adjustments with base-velocity commands. Multi-objective rewards penalize bimanual internal opposition, grasp slip, and actuator saturation, encouraging the policy to apply contact force on demand without human demonstrations. Sim-to-sim experiments show that ForPC reduces cart-velocity RMSE by up to 68.2% relative to a locomotion-only baseline (Loco-only) and cross-track RMSE by up to 74.2% on the multi-bend route. Trained solely in simulation, the policy also transfers to a physical Unitree G1 without real-world training or fine-tuning and, with no payload-specific adjustment, pushes a cart carrying up to 30 kg at 0.5 m/s. These results suggest that humanoid robots could eventually replace humans for efficient material handling in daily life.

papers.title: Compressed Per-Player Local Methods for Multiplayer Federated Learning: Exact Convergence via Increment Sharing
papers.summary: Multiplayer Federated Learning (MpFL), introduced by Yoon et al. (2025), extends classical federated learning to settings where clients are rational players in a game with individual objectives and strategies, seeking an equilibrium. A natural baseline is Per-Player Local SGD (PEARL-SGD), where each player performs several local SGD steps before exchanging strategies through a central server. However, the original PEARL-SGD formulation does not extend cleanly to compressed communication. Directly compressing the players' strategies can prevent convergence to the equilibrium, even with deterministic gradients. To address this issue, we reformulate PEARL-SGD so that players communicate local strategy increments rather than the strategies themselves. Without compression, the two formulations are equivalent, but with compression, increment sharing preserves exact convergence, allowing us to design the communication-efficient compressed PEARL-SGD (C-PEARL-SGD). Beyond compression, we also consider variance reduction as another axis of improvement, introducing PEARL-SVRG and its compressed variant C-PEARL-SVRG. Under the original MpFL assumptions, we establish convergence guarantees for all variants through a unified parametric inequality. Numerical experiments, including distributed spectrum sensing, demonstrate the practical benefits of our methods over vanilla PEARL-SGD.
papers.title_ja: マルチプレイヤー連合学習のための圧縮されたプレイヤー別ローカル手法：増分共有による厳密な収束
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、マルチプレイヤー連合学習（MpFL）における通信効率化と収束性の両立を提案する。従来の戦略直接共有方式では圧縮通信により収束が阻害される問題に対し、プレイヤーがローカル戦略の増分を共有する方式に定式化し直すことで、圧縮下でも均衡への厳密な収束を保証する。さらに分散低減手法（SVRG）との統合により、C-PEARL-SGD や C-PEARL-SVRG を提案し、統一されたパラメトリック不等式を用いて収束性を理論的に証明した。数値実験では、分散スペクトラムセンシングなどの応用において、既存手法より優れた性能を実証している。

papers.title: Does a Trading Policy Need to Know What It Trades? Microstructure Invariance and Zero-Shot Transfer of Execution Policies
papers.summary: Execution algorithms are calibrated asset by asset, because the queues, trade rates and bid-ask spreads they face differ by orders of magnitude across assets. For reinforcement learning this is zero-shot generalisation across contexts of very different scales, and microstructure invariance proposes a normalisation fixed by theory: measured in each asset's own units of time, size and price, markets look alike. In an exact order-by-order replay of public Nasdaq data, we train policies once, on 954 stocks in 2019, to choose between waiting in the queue and crossing the spread, and evaluate them unchanged on 1,964 unseen stocks in 2020-21, 2,629 stocks in 2025-26, crypto pairs and a second exchange. First, a policy that sees a stock only through its recent trade rate, trade size, spread and price increment (tick) costs within 0.015 spreads per share (a fifth of what learning saves) of a policy whose training data included the stock, and the stock's own history does not help it; it comes within a similar margin of policies trained on the second exchange when every episode counts equally, and within a wider one on crypto. Second, in mean cost before fees, invariant units beat raw units, z-scores and asset descriptors, but by under a basis point: most of their advantage is information and a common cost scale that a learner can also take as plain inputs, and none of the representations tested extrapolates to unseen spread regimes. Third, a near-zero transfer gap to a pooled comparator is weak evidence that a representation is right: we show that such a comparator detects only a small share of what a poor representation loses, and confirm it in synthetic markets and on pendulums.
papers.title_ja: 取引ポリシーは取引対象を知る必要があるのか？マイクロストラクチャ不変性と執行ポリシーのゼロショット転移

papers.title: Robust Adaptive Lyapunov-Based MPC for Nonlinear Systems with Experimental Validation on Quadcopter Attitude Control
papers.summary: In this paper, a computationally efficient robust adaptive Lyapunov-based model predictive control (RALMPC) framework is proposed for a class of constrained nonlinear systems subject to uncertainties and external disturbances. A radial basis function neural network (RBFNN), introduced to approximate non-parametric uncertainties, is incorporated into a control Lyapunov function analysis, together with integral barrier Lyapunov functionals for state constraint enforcement. This analysis yields control and adaptation laws for parametric uncertainties, external disturbances, RBFNN weights, and worst-case approximation error, rendering the closed-loop system uniformly bounded while ensuring convergence of tracking errors to compact sets around the origin. The resulting guarantees are then embedded into the RALMPC optimal control problem through a contractive constraint, thus combining formal closed-loop stability with real-time performance optimization; at the same time, the adaptation laws allow the RALMPC prediction model to be updated online. Comparative hardware-in-the-loop simulations against state-of-the-art MPC schemes validate the efficacy and computational efficiency of the proposed framework. Ultimately, RALMPC is experimentally validated on a custom-built quadcopter platform for time-varying attitude tracking, demonstrating its practical feasibility; comparisons against alternative strategies confirm its superiority in achieving improved closed-loop performance.
papers.title_ja: 四回転翼機姿勢制御の実験検証を伴う、非線形システム向けの頑健適応型リャプノフベースMPC
papers.summary_ja: 不確実性と外部擾乱を持つ非線形システム向けに、計算効率の高い頑健適応型モデル予測制御（RALMPC）フレームワークを提案する。ラジアルベース関数ニューラルネットワーク（RBFNN）を用いて非パラメトリックな不確実性を近似し、制御リャプノフ関数と積分バリアリャプノフ関数を組み合わせた解析により、閉ループ系の安定性と状態制約の強制を理論的に保証する。この保証を収縮制約としてMPCの最適化問題に埋め込むことで、形式安定性とリアルタイム性能の両立を実現し、オンラインでのモデル更新も可能にする。ハードウェアインザループシミュレーションおよび自作四回転翼機を用いた実験により、既存手法に対する計算効率と制御性能の優位性を検証した。

papers.title: Cutpurse: Decomposing Explanation-Guided Model Extraction on Tabular Data
papers.summary: Explanation APIs are often treated as increasing model-extraction risk, but an end-to-end attack comparison cannot show whether an explanation reveals model-specific information or merely supplies a convenient next-query coordinate. We study this distinction for explanation-guided extraction of tabular classifiers. We separate an explanation into an attribution channel, which ranks influential features, and a coordinate channel, which supplies candidate feature values for perturbing those features. We then test whether the useful bin edges are privileged to the service or reproducible from the adversary's own data. Across six datasets and five target families, using attribution rankings to choose which features to perturb provides no systematic extraction advantage. Lime's discretization bin edges can improve fidelity by up to 41 percentage points on continuous features, but those edges are quantiles of the explainer's background data rather than properties of the target model. In controlled comparisons, an attacker-side grid reproduces the useful bin-edge gains without querying an explanation API. We use these findings to derive Cutpurse, which combines a self-computed grid with diverse query generation and boundary search. Against a service that withholds bin edges, Cutpurse improves fidelity by 16.3 percentage points on continuous-feature targets. It also exceeds the undefended published attack by 7.0 percentage points. Thus, withholding default Lime bin edges alone does not prevent effective extraction under the in-domain auxiliary-input, probability-output, and same-family surrogate assumptions studied here. Our results concern default Lime and Shap configurations for tabular classifiers. They do not establish the same conclusion for other explainers, target classes, or data-free attackers.

papers.summary_ja: 表形式分類器に対する説明APIを用いたモデル抽出攻撃を分析し、説明が提供する「重要度ランキング」と「候補値（座標）」の役割を分離した。重要度ランキング自体は抽出効率に系統的な優位性を与えない一方、LIMEの離散化境界値は忠実度を最大41ポイント向上させる可能性があるが、これはターゲットモデル固有の情報ではなく背景データ由来であることが判明した。攻撃者側でグリッドを自己計算することで同等の効果を再現可能であり、境界値を非公開にしても防御にはならないことを示した。

papers.title: Drift-admissibility via Optimal Transport
papers.summary: We introduce structure-aware optimal transport diagnostics for assessing whether empirical time-series dynamics are compatible with a prescribed predictable-drift class. Our approach translates a pathwise property of stochastic processes into a finite-dimensional projection problem over empirical transition laws, encoding admissibility as row-wise moment constraints on local couplings and quantifying deviations via a Kullback--Leibler projection gap $G_{\lambda,k}$. This yields both a principled diagnostic and a scalable Bregman--Dykstra algorithm that retains the efficiency of Sinkhorn-type methods while incorporating structural constraints. Calibrated against a Brownian reference null, $G_{\lambda,k}$ separates process classes that are indistinguishable by second-order statistics alone---including fractional Brownian motion and BSS processes sharing identical Hurst indices---without asymptotic resampling or continuous-time recovery. This positions the method as a general tool for structure-aware model validation of sequential data.
papers.title_ja: 最適輸送によるドリフト許容性の判定

papers.title: Transporting the Past: An Optimal Transport View of Backtracking Counterfactuals
papers.summary: We study backtracking counterfactual inference for Structural Causal Models (SCMs) through the lens of optimal transport. In SCMs, a factual observation generally induces a posterior distribution over exogenous variables, making counterfactual inference inherently distributional. We introduce two complementary frameworks that transport this posterior onto the set of exogenous configurations satisfying a desired counterfactual query. The first constructs a natural pointwise projection and is suitable when the transported exogenous distribution can be used directly. The second enforces mutual independence among counterfactual exogenous variables, so that the transported variables remain interpretable as genuine exogenous noises of the same SCM. We show that both frameworks are consistent with the original backtracking counterfactual principle, and we propose marginal, penalty-based, and hard-constrained solvers for finite-posterior settings. Synthetic experiments on non-bijective SCMs illustrate the geometry of the problem and reveal trade-offs among transport cost, counterfactual constraint satisfaction, and preservation of exogenous independence.
papers.title_ja: 過去を輸送する：バックトラッキング反事実の最適輸送による視点

papers.title: VICTR: Value-Informed In-Context Learning for Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.summary: Recent advances in robot foundation models have highlighted the potential of in-context learning (ICL) for adapting robot behavior from demonstrations without further fine-tuning. Previous work has used retrieval-based post-training to equip pretrained vision-language-action (VLA) models with the capability for ICL by teaching them to condition action predictions on retrieved visually-relevant demonstration chunks. However, the effectiveness of retrieval hinges on selecting context relevant to the current execution stage, which visual similarity alone may not capture. We introduce VICTR, a framework enabling in-context learning in VLAs via progress-informed context retrieval built around an In-Context Value Function Estimator (IC-VFE). IC-VFE conditions on a reference demonstration video, a language instruction and the current observation to estimate task-relative progress. By conditioning progress estimation on a reference demonstration, IC-VFE can align the current state with a demonstrated execution even for tasks unseen during training. VICTR uses the estimated progress to select demonstration chunks at corresponding stages of execution and supplies them to a $\pi_{0.5}$ policy post-trained for in-context action generation. On unseen out-of-domain real-world manipulation tasks, VICTR raises the success rate from 6.2% for a fine-tuned $\pi_{0.5}$ baseline to 23.8% and more than doubles the task progress rate, from 28.9% to 55.5%. Project page with code, data and videos: https://ai4ce.github.io/VICTR/

papers.summary_ja: ロボット操作におけるインコンテキスト学習（ICL）の精度向上を目的としたフレームワークVICTRを提案する。視覚的類似性だけでなく、タスクの進行度合い（プログレス）を推定する価値関数評価器（IC-VFE）を導入し、現在の状態に最も関連するデモチャンクを検索・選択する。これにより、未見の操作タスクでも適切な文脈を提示し、アクション生成の成功率と進行率を大幅に向上させる。

papers.title: Foundation-Model Residuals as Signals of Urban Bus Irregularity
papers.summary: Pretrained trajectory models encode mobility patterns learned across cities, but their errors when transferred to a new city are usually treated only as performance limitations. We instead ask whether these residuals reveal systematic local conditions. Architectures such as UniTraj and TrajFM learn transferable trajectory representations, although cross-context transfer remains challenging. Using the NetMob26 bus location, ticketing, weather, network, and socioeconomic data for Niteroi, we analyze spatial and travel-time residuals of these recent trajectory foundation models. We test whether high residuals concentrate spatially, whether spatial and travel-time residuals overlap, and which urban-context variables explain their distribution. We interpret high residuals as candidate proxy signals of transit irregularity rather than direct evidence of service disruption, and analyze their contextual associations using Explainable AI (XAI). Insights into such varied environments are increasingly valuable for evaluating new urban paradigms; for instance, the 15-minute-city perspective serves as a key motivation for our approach, guiding our methods and expanding the analysis beyond standard mobility metrics.

papers.title: LeanDojo-v2: A Comprehensive Library for AI-Assisted Theorem Proving in Lean
papers.summary: Building on recent progress in machine learning for formal theorem proving in Lean, we introduce LeanDojo-v2: an end-to-end framework that unifies repository data extraction, LLM fine-tuning, proof search, AI autocompletion, and LLM-assisted theorem proving in a single software library. In addition, we provide Lean4Code, a lightweight IDE that integrates the various features of LeanDojo-v2 through a simple, mathematician-friendly UI. These tools will enable mathematicians and researchers to easily fine-tune language models on domain-specific Lean codebases and experiment with LLM-assisted theorem proving without a complex setup.

papers.title: Advances in High-Precision Astrometry for Exoplanet Detection for Astrometric Missions
papers.summary: High-precision astrometry is a cornerstone for detecting Earth-like exoplanets in the habitable zones of nearby solar-type stars and probing the nature of dark matter in galactic environments. Achieving sub-microarcsecond accuracy requires unprecedented control over detector morphology, optical distortion, and astrometric measurement techniques. This paper reviews recent progress in characterizing large format detector at the micropixel scale level, calibrating optical distortion using reference stars, and refining differential astrometry methods to detect the faint astrometric signatures of Earth-mass exoplanets. We highlight the latest developments in the RETINA project, which aims to advance the TRL of GIGAPYX 220 MP CMOS detectors from Pyxalis which are critical components for future space missions such as ESA's Theia and NASA's Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO). The project focuses on precise calibration methods, including Young's fringe projection, to monitor pixel geometry and intra-pixel response across gigapixel-scale focal planes. By integrating these advancements, RETINA seeks to enable astrometric detection of Earth-mass exoplanets with a precision of few tens of micropixels on the focal plane. We discuss the technical strategies, laboratory validations, and system-level integration required to achieve these goals, emphasizing the synergy between detector technology, optical calibration, and mission design. These innovations pave the way for next-generation astrometric instruments capable of transforming our understanding of exoplanetary systems and dark matter dynamics.
papers.title_ja: 系外惑星検出のための高精度天体測位技術の進歩：天体測位ミッション向け
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、近傍太陽型恒星のハビタブルゾーンにおける地球型系外惑星の検出と暗黒物質の探査を目的とした、サブマイクロアーク秒精度の天体測位技術の最新進展をレビューする。ピクセルスケールでの大面積検出器の特性評価、基準星を用いた光学歪みの較正、および微分天体測位手法の改良に焦点を当てる。特に、ESAのTheiaやNASAのHWOなどの将来ミッションで重要なGIGAPYX 220 MP CMOS検出器の技術成熟度（TRL）向上を目指すRETINAプロジェクトの詳細を解説する。Youngの縞投射法によるピクセル幾何学とピクセル内応答の監視など、ギガピクセル規模の焦点面での精密較正手法と、地球質量級惑星の検出を可能にするシステム統合戦略を議論する。

papers.title: Autonomous Whole-body Loco-manipulation Using a Snake Robot
papers.summary: Snake robots can leverage their hyper-redundant morphology for both locomotion and manipulation through distributed body contact but whole-body loco-manipulation is particularly challenging since the entire body serves simultaneously as propulsive mechanism and manipulation tool Prior work on wheeled legged and snake robot platforms has decoupled these functions through dedicated appendages body segmentation or grippers We present closed-loop loco-manipulation with our snake robot COBRA without this distinction such that any part of the body may make contact We develop a contact-implicit dynamic model unifying robot-ground robot-object and object-ground interactions within a Moreau-Jean time-stepping framework and formulate a trajectory optimization over the full-order dynamics guided by a geometric planner and nominal proportional controller to autonomously push an object to a goal location during sidewinding We validate the planner and controller on hardware across varied configurations and present simulation results for a simplified trajectory optimization that resolves robot-object and object-ground contacts
papers.title_ja: ヘビ型ロボットを用いた自律的な全身ローコマニピュレーション

papers.title: Different exact-law formulations to calculate the energy cascade rate in magnetohydrodynamic turbulence with and without mean magnetic fields
papers.summary: At scales much larger than the ion inertial length and ion-gyroscale, space-plasma turbulence is often described within the framework of incompressible magnetohydrodynamics (MHD). Using high-resolution direct numerical simulations with $1024^3$ grid points, we perform the first systematic numerical comparison of three exact-law formulations for the total energy cascade in homogeneous, but not necessarily isotropic, MHD turbulence: the Yaglom-Monin (YM), Banerjee-Galtier (BG), and two-point correlator formulations. Despite directional variations, the angle-averaged energy transfer rates for all three formulations show excellent agreement for zero, moderate, and strong background magnetic fields. These results clearly suggest the usefulness of alternative BG and correlator formulations for estimating the energy cascade rates in turbulent space plasmas when the required spatial derivatives are accessible through multi-spacecraft measurements. We also argue that the isotropic Politano-Pouquet (PP) formulation does not provide a true directional transfer rate and therefore its application as a single-direction energy transfer rate estimator leads to inaccurate values, especially under anisotropic conditions. Decomposing the exact formulations into RMHD and non-RMHD contributions, we also show that the RMHD cascade rates cannot be obtained merely by increasing the strength of the mean magnetic field in incompressible magnetohydrodynamic turbulence. Finally, a term-by-term analysis of different formulations reveals how different nonlinear interaction channels coexist and collaborate with each other to maintain the same energy cascade rate across the inertial scales.

papers.title: Effects of a Nuclear Detonation in Low Earth Orbit
papers.summary: More than 13,000 satellites operate in low Earth orbit (LEO), and concern has grown that nuclear weapons could be used in space to target them. Beyond the initial X-ray burst, electrons released by radioactive fission products can become trapped in Earth's magnetic field, repeatedly exposing satellites as an artificial radiation belt. Here we couple prompt radiation, electron trapping and belt evolution to satellite failures, collisions and atmospheric drag. For a 1-Mt detonation at 500km over the South Atlantic, repeated belt exposure disables approximately 98% of modeled satellites within one week in our central case. Tripling the assumed radiation tolerance delays widespread failure by only days: approximately 97% are still disabled within two weeks. The loss of maneuverability sharply increases collision risk, with approximately 20 collisions expected within two years. Drag removes many disabled spacecraft from lower altitudes, but replacement satellites could remain exposed to radiation and debris for years. These findings show how a single detonation could devastate orbital infrastructure and support efforts to prevent the deployment and use of nuclear weapons in space.

papers.title: On the Incompleteness of do-calculus for Universal Identifiability
papers.summary: We study the problem of causal effect identification from an arbitrary set of observational and/or interventional distributions, which we call Universal Identifiability (uID). The uID problem generalizes existing classical identifiability (ID) and general identifiability (gID) problems, which considered the identification problem from either mere observational distributions or a specific type of interventional distributions. Prior research has established graphical criteria to determine when a causal effect is identifiable in ID and gID problems. Moreover, algorithms that leverage do-calculus and basic probability manipulations have been proposed to compute these effects. Consequently, it has been shown that do-calculus is both sound and complete in these problems. Despite these well-established results, a formal definition of what it means for the do-calculus to be complete does not exist. We propose a rigorous formalization for the completeness of the do-calculus and show that the completeness results in previous work remain valid. However, for more general problems, such as uID, the rules of do-calculus are no longer complete. This is perhaps the reason why the uID problem has remained open thus far.

papers.title: On Differentially Private Mechanisms for Linear Regression
papers.summary: We study the classic least-squares linear regression problem under differential privacy (DP) in the batch and the continual observation setting. In the latter setting, the mechanism receives a stream of $n$ data points $(x_i,y_i)$ ($x_i\in\mathbb{R}^d$ and $y_i\in\mathbb{R}$) and must output an estimate of the optimal parameters at each time step $i$. Although differentially private linear regression has been extensively studied in the batch setting, the problem remains underexplored for the continual setting, with prior work being restricted to constrained linear regression and update time polynomial in $n$. In this work, we introduce ContinualAdaSSP, the first mechanism for unconstrained linear regression under continual differential privacy. Our mechanism's suboptimality gap is proportional to $\sqrt{d}\operatorname{polylog}(n)$. It requires $O(d^2\log{n})$ space and $O(d^2\log{n}+d^{\omega})$ update time, where $d$ is the dimension of the input space. We also study fundamental limits of differentially private linear regression by showing the first lower bounds for the box-constrained least-squares linear regression problem. Our lower bounds are proportional to $\min(n,\frac{\sqrt{d}}{\log^{1.5}d})$ for $(1,O(\frac{1}{n}))$-DP, and $\min(n,\frac{d}{\epsilon})$ for $\epsilon$-DP, and are derived using a reduction from a fingerprinting code problem from [Peter et al., 2024], providing new insights into the inherent hardness of this canonical task. Our experimental evaluation on real-world datasets shows that the accuracy of our continual observation mechanism clearly outperforms any other known differentially private mechanism for this problem such as rerunning the batch algorithm at each time step.
